title: Cold Chain Reset
note: МАКЕТ. Сценарий, тексты и веса — наши. Ни одного числа, имени и формулировки PrepMatter (Ф3). Развилки ветвят по РОДУ хода, а не по его качеству (Ф21).

intro.head: Welcome to the Sustainable Futures Lab
intro.body: You have joined a small team advising a regional food distributor. You will make thirteen decisions. There is one clock for all of them, and you cannot go back.

intro.head: Background
intro.body: Vantefjord Provisions moves chilled produce from four hundred small farms to two hundred shops. Most of the cold chain is not theirs: the farms own their own chillers, and about half of those units run on a refrigerant that must be out of service in three years under a phase-down the company cannot influence. A unit costs a farm roughly two months of its margin to replace. Vantefjord buys from these farms but does not own them, has no contract term that compels an upgrade, and loses the produce anyway if a chiller fails in August.
intro.mission: Your mission: have the cold chain running on compliant refrigerant in three years, without losing farms you cannot replace.

priorities.label: Get the four hundred farms moving, since the equipment is theirs and not yours
Form a view on which upgrade path is affordable at farm scale
Find out which chillers are actually non-compliant and where they are
Agree with your own board what the company will pay for and what it will not

steps.prompt: Put these four actions in the order you would take them, starting with the one you would do first.
steps.why: Здесь первым идёт разговор с фермами, и это не вежливость, а арифметика. Оборудование принадлежит четырёмстам независимым хозяйствам, у компании нет ни договорного рычага, ни собственности — значит любое решение исполняется только их руками и только добровольно. Четыреста хозяйств физически невозможно обойти быстро: это самая длинная операция в проекте и единственная, которую нельзя ускорить деньгами. Инвентаризация (D) при этом собирается ровно в тех же визитах — отдельной кампанией она стоит вдвое дороже и приезжает позже. Согласование с советом (A) идёт последним намеренно: пока неизвестно, сколько ферм согласны и на что, любая цифра, вынесенная на совет, — это выдумка, а выдумку, однажды одобренную, потом придётся защищать.

feedback.top: Your order starts with the only party that can actually replace a chiller, and the survey rides along with the same visits. Everything else in this project is faster than four hundred conversations.
feedback.mid: Your order is defensible, but it puts analysis ahead of the four hundred visits that set the true length of the project.
feedback.low: Your order settles the company's position before anyone has asked a farmer anything. You will be defending a number to your board that nobody outside the building has agreed to.

steps.prompt: You cannot visit four hundred farms yourself inside any useful timeframe. The distributor has eleven field buyers who already visit every farm on a fortnightly cycle.

options.text: You train the eleven buyers to run the conversation on their existing rounds, and go with each of them once, since the visit already happens.
options.fb: Four hundred farms are unreachable to you and routine to them. Riding along once with each buyer is what stops the training becoming a form that gets filled in the van afterwards.

options.text: You hire a survey firm to cover all four hundred farms in six weeks, so the data arrives fast, uniform and in one format rather than eleven.
options.fb: Six weeks and clean data is a real advantage, and a stranger with a clipboard gets a different answer from a farm than the buyer who has been coming for nine years.

options.text: You send the buyers a questionnaire to hand out, since they are already going anyway and their time is expensive.
options.fb: A questionnaire handed over in a doorway measures who fills in questionnaires. The point of using the buyers was the conversation, not the delivery.

options.text: You start with the sixty largest farms yourself, since they carry most of the volume, and reach the rest later.
options.fb: Sensible triage on volume, and the failure that spoils a lorry is just as likely in a small chiller. You have covered the tonnage and not the risk.

steps.prompt: The first hundred surveys come back. Sixty-one farms report a compliant refrigerant, thirty-two report the phased-down one, and seven do not know. The buyers note that several of the sixty-one read the answer off a sticker rather than a nameplate.

options.text: You treat sticker-sourced answers as unknown and have the buyers photograph nameplates on the next round.
options.fb: A sticker records what someone believed at installation; a nameplate records what is in the unit. Turning a soft answer into a missing one is what keeps the count honest as it grows.

options.text: You accept the reported figures and apply the seven per cent unknown rate to the remaining three hundred as a planning assumption.
options.fb: You have carried forward a proportion drawn from answers you were just told are unreliable, which makes the projection confident and wrong in the same step.

options.text: You send a technician to re-verify a sample of twenty of the sixty-one compliant answers before deciding what to do about the rest.
options.fb: A sample tells you how wrong the stickers are, which is worth knowing. It also costs a technician's fortnight to measure an error you can simply eliminate on the next visit.

options.text: You drop the self-reported data entirely and put a technician on every farm, on the view that a question about equipment deserves an answer from somebody who can open the unit.
options.fb: Four hundred technician visits is the most accurate survey nobody will finish in time, and it takes the buyers out of a conversation the project needs them inside.

steps.prompt: Two routes to compliance are open and you can develop one properly this quarter. They differ in kind: one changes what the farms own, the other changes where the cooling happens.

options.text: You develop farm-level replacement: a financed swap of each non-compliant unit, priced so the repayment sits below what the farm already spends on running the old one.
options.fb: Replacement keeps the cold chain where it is and asks each farm for a decision it can afford on its own terms. Pricing against their current running cost is what turns an obligation into an offer.

options.text: You develop shared cooling: four regional chilled hubs owned by the distributor, with farms delivering warm and the company taking the refrigerant problem in-house.
options.fb: Taking the problem in-house solves compliance for four hundred farms in four buildings, which is a genuinely different answer. It also moves cost, risk and an extra handling step onto the company.

options.text: You spend the quarter costing the penalty for missing the phase-down, so the board can compare compliance with the price of not complying, and leave the hub outline standing as the alternative.
options.fb: The phase-down is a date in law, not a tariff the company can elect to pay. You spent the only quarter you had developing an option the board cannot take, and the outline went up unexamined.

B1a.prompt: The financed swap works on paper for farms above a certain size. Below it, the repayment exceeds the running-cost saving, and about a hundred and forty farms sit below that line.

options.text: You publish the offer for the farms it works for and say that a hundred and forty need a different answer you have not found yet.
options.fb: Shipping the part that works starts two hundred and sixty upgrades this year. Naming the gap yourself is what stops those hundred and forty finding out by applying and being refused.

options.text: You hold the offer until the arithmetic works for every farm on the list, so that nobody is told in writing that they do not qualify for the company's own programme.
options.fb: Fair in intent, and it costs the farms who could have started a year of the three you have. Waiting for a universal answer is a decision about them made without them.

options.text: You stretch the repayment period until the arithmetic works for the smallest farm, and apply the same terms to everybody.
options.fb: The arithmetic now works because the debt outlives the equipment. You have solved the presentation of the problem and lengthened the problem itself.

B1b.prompt: The hub option is the one that reaches the board, and it moves a cost the farms were carrying onto the company's balance sheet: roughly the equivalent of a fifth of the distributor's annual operating profit, every year, permanently.

options.text: You put the hubs forward as a change to what the company is, not as a compliance measure, and ask the board to decide on that basis.
options.fb: A permanent fifth of operating profit is a decision about the business model, and framing it as a refrigerant project would get it approved by people answering a smaller question.

options.text: You present the hubs as the compliance solution with the cost shown in the appendix. Compliance is not optional.
options.fb: Compliance is not optional and this particular route to it very much is. The appendix is where a decision goes to be approved without being taken.

options.text: You propose two hubs instead of four, covering the densest half of the farms, and revisit the rest later.
options.fb: Halving the commitment while the model is unproven is a real answer. It also leaves half the farms with the original problem and the company with a second decision it has not framed.

steps.prompt: The board will fund a subsidy, but wants it tied to exclusivity: a farm that takes the money agrees to sell only to Vantefjord for five years. Several of the largest farms have always sold to two buyers.

options.text: You tie the subsidy to the equipment rather than the relationship: repayable in full if the farm sells the unit or leaves, because the money is for the unit.
options.fb: The board's real interest is not being funded and then abandoned, and that interest survives without an exclusivity clause. You protected the money and left the farm its second buyer.

options.text: You accept exclusivity, since the company is putting up the capital and has a right to secure the supply it is paying to protect.
options.fb: The clause is defensible and the farms most able to refuse it are the ones carrying the most volume. You will lose the argument with exactly the suppliers you cannot replace.

options.text: You argue against attaching any condition at all, since the phase-down is a problem the whole supply chain shares and every clause you add is a reason for a farm to wait another year.
options.fb: Uptake matters, and a subsidy with no strings is a grant the board did not agree to make. You are asking them to trust four hundred parties they have no relationship with.

steps.prompt: At the first regional meeting, a farmer who has supplied the company for twenty-two years says the phase-down is being used as cover to push small farms out, and the room goes quiet in a way that suggests agreement.

options.text: You answer that the concern is reasonable, give the number of farms below the affordability line, and say what you have and have not solved for them.
options.fb: The room went quiet because the accusation matched their arithmetic. Giving them the number you already know is the only answer that is not a reassurance, and reassurance is what they were expecting.

options.text: You explain that the phase-down is regulatory, applies to everyone equally, and is entirely outside the company's control.
options.fb: Every word is accurate and it answers a question about the regulation while they asked a question about you.

options.text: You commit on the spot, in front of the whole room, that no farm will be dropped for having a non-compliant chiller.
options.fb: The commitment is the right instinct and you have just made it for a company whose board has not agreed it. A promise you cannot bank is worth one meeting.

options.text: You take the point away and offer to come back to the region with a specific answer for farms under the line.
options.fb: Returning with an answer is better than improvising one, and leaving the room without saying anything true today means the accusation stands until you come back.

steps.prompt: Eighteen months in, a competitor announces it will fund chiller replacement for any farm in the region, with no conditions at all. Two of your largest suppliers ask what you intend to do about it. There are two different kinds of answer.

options.text: You answer on the merits of your own offer, setting out what it gives a farm that theirs does not, and put the two side by side for the farms to read.
options.fb: A comparison the farm can check itself is the only response that survives their announcement being better than yours in one respect. You also stopped competing on the single dimension where you cannot win.

options.text: You go to the board for authority to match the unconditional terms before any farm decides, since the first mover sets what the rest expect.
options.fb: Matching is a legitimate answer and it is a different game: you are now bidding for suppliers rather than solving a phase-down, and the bidding has no natural end.

options.text: You wait to see how many farms actually take the competitor's offer before responding. An announcement is not a signed agreement and nobody has counted the takers yet.
options.fb: By the time the number is known, the farms who moved have moved, and you will be responding to a fact instead of a choice.

B2a.prompt: Three months later, uptake of your offer is running at seventy per cent among farms the buyers visited in person and at nineteen per cent among those who received it by post. Both groups were meant to be randomly assigned.

options.text: You check how the assignment was actually done before concluding anything about visits, because a gap that size usually means the groups differ.
options.fb: A fifty-point gap is too large for the visit alone, and the likeliest explanation is that the buyers went to the farms they expected to say yes. Checking the assignment costs a day and decides where the next year's effort goes.

options.text: You take the result at face value and move the whole rollout to in-person visits, since a gap this wide makes the self-reported figures look unusable.
options.fb: You have committed eleven buyers for a year on the strength of a comparison that was never a comparison.

options.text: You run the postal group again with a better letter, since the difference may be the writing rather than the channel.
options.fb: The letter may well be part of it, and testing it before you know whether the groups were comparable means a good result will be just as unreadable as this one.

B2b.prompt: The board authorises matching the competitor's terms, and the finance team's model shows the matched offer paying for itself through retained volume. The retention figure in the model is the one your own team supplied, from farms who had already said they were staying.

options.text: You flag that the retention figure came from farms never at risk, since a model answers only the question its inputs asked.
options.fb: A business case that answers itself is worse than no business case, because it will be quoted for years. The farms who were always staying cannot tell you what retention costs.

options.text: You let the model stand. The number is genuine, came from real farms, and re-running it costs a month the competitor is spending on the same suppliers.
options.fb: The number is genuine about a population that is not the one in question, and your name is on the input.

options.text: You add a sensitivity range around the retention figure so that the board can see how much of the case rests on that single number holding.
options.fb: A range is honest arithmetic on a dishonest population. It shows how wrong the answer could be without saying that the question was asked of the wrong farms.

steps.prompt: With nine months to the deadline, roughly ninety farms still run non-compliant units. Buying them all out costs about a tenth of the programme budget; dropping them costs about four per cent of volume, concentrated in one region.

options.text: You take the buy-out to the board as the cost of the position the company has held with these farms since the programme began.
options.fb: The programme has run on the understanding that it was not pushing these farms out, and a tenth of the budget is what that understanding costs. Naming it as the price of a position already taken is what gets it approved.

options.text: You drop the ninety, since four per cent of volume is recoverable and a tenth of the budget is not.
options.fb: Four per cent of volume in one region is most of one region's farms, and the phase-down will have done exactly what the farmer said it would.

options.text: You buy out the forty largest of the ninety and let the rest lapse.
options.fb: It halves the bill and it also selects by size for the first time in the programme — after two years of insisting that size was not the criterion.

options.text: You ask the regulator whether a short extension is available for farms below a size threshold, since the phase-down was written for industrial refrigeration rather than for four hundred smallholdings.
options.fb: Worth asking, and the answer arrives on the regulator's timetable rather than yours. It is a good second move and a poor first one.

steps.prompt: The installer says the remaining farms fit inside the phase-down date only if sign-off gets lighter, and he is willing to discuss where. Today a technician verifies every installation on site. The regulator audits refrigerant handover documents; it has never asked to see an installation certificate.

options.text: You keep technician sign-off on the refrigerant handover and take the farm's own form for the rest of the installation.
options.fb: You split the sign-off along the line the regulator actually reads. The document it audits keeps a qualified signature, the part nobody audits gets the cheap process, and the installer has the relief he asked for.

options.text: You keep technician sign-off on everything and accept that the last farms run into the harvest fortnight.
options.fb: Clean and expensive. Every certificate is worth what it says, and you have moved the finish into the two weeks when nobody on a farm has time for you.

options.text: You accept the farm's own form for everything, since the regulator has never asked for the certificate.
options.fb: Never asked is not the same as will not ask, and refrigerant handover is exactly where an audit starts. You traded the one document that gets read.

options.text: You accept the farm's own form and add a sample audit of one farm in ten after the deadline.
options.fb: A sample after the date tells you how many are wrong when it is too late to be right. The audit is real work with no route back to compliance.

steps.prompt: Six weeks before the deadline, the installer tells you they can finish on time only by working through the harvest fortnight, when the farms are least able to give access. Two ways out, and they are different in kind.

options.text: You go to the farms and ask which of them can take an installation during harvest, and build the schedule from who volunteers.
options.fb: The farms know their own fortnight better than any scheduler, and asking turns an imposition into a queue. It also surfaces the ones who genuinely cannot, before the installer arrives to find nobody home.

options.text: You add a second installation crew for the final six weeks, funded from the contingency, so harvest can be worked around entirely.
options.fb: Money for time is the cleanest trade available here and it is not free: a crew hired for six weeks arrives without the relationships the first one built over two years.

options.text: You instruct the installer to work through harvest and notify the farms of their appointed slots.
options.fb: Two years of asking, and the last six weeks tell the farms what the relationship was actually worth.

B3a.prompt: Enough farms volunteer to make the schedule work, but eleven of them cannot take an installation before the deadline under any arrangement. All eleven have been supplying the company for more than a decade.

options.text: You disclose the eleven to the regulator before the deadline, with the dates they will be completed and why.
options.fb: A disclosed shortfall with a date is a compliance conversation; the same shortfall found in an audit is an enforcement one. Eleven farms is small enough to be forgiven and large enough not to hide.

options.text: You suspend purchasing from the eleven on the deadline and resume once they are converted.
options.fb: You have made eleven long-standing suppliers carry the consequence of a schedule they offered to accommodate, and every other farm in the region will hear about it.

options.text: You complete the programme, report full compliance, and finish the eleven quietly in the weeks after.
options.fb: The report is false on the day it is signed, and the eleven farms are witnesses to that fact for as long as the paperwork exists.

B3b.prompt: Installation runs through the harvest fortnight one way or another, and in the final week the crew tells you that a batch of the new units was commissioned without the pressure test the manufacturer specifies. They cannot say which farms.

options.text: You stop signing off the programme, have the manufacturer define what identifies an untested unit, and re-test everything that fits.
options.fb: «Cannot say which» is not a small subset of the problem, it is the whole of it. Letting the manufacturer set the identifying test is how the retest becomes finite instead of four hundred.

options.text: You re-test a representative sample of the batch and, if it passes, sign off the programme on the strength of it rather than holding four hundred farms for a fault nobody has seen.
options.fb: A passing sample tells you the failure is not universal. It does not tell any individual farm that the unit in their yard was tested, and that is the question they will ask in August.

options.text: You sign off on the deadline and schedule the retests as post-installation maintenance. The units are installed and the compliance date is the thing the regulator counts.
options.fb: You have converted a known defect into a maintenance item on your own authority, and dated the signature before the check.

axis.none: замер круга 40: во всём видимом тексте нет ни одного числа с единицей — объявлять нечего. Это не освобождение: класс G краснеет, как только величина заведётся.

title: Peatland Baseline
note: МАКЕТ. Сценарий, тексты и веса — наши. Ни одного числа, имени и формулировки PrepMatter (Ф3). Развилки ветвят по РОДУ хода (Ф21).

intro.head: Welcome to the Sustainable Futures Lab
intro.body: You have joined a small team advising a landed estate. You will make thirteen decisions. There is one clock for all of them, and you cannot go back.

intro.head: Background
intro.body: Ardvane Estate holds four thousand hectares of peatland drained for grazing in the nineteen-sixties. Blocking the drains would raise the water table within weeks and turn the bog from a carbon source into a carbon sink, and a buyer has offered to purchase the verified units on delivery in three years. Verification requires a measured baseline of the drained state across a full year, including one dry summer. The blocking itself is a single three-week operation across the whole estate — there is no version of it that leaves part of the ground drained, because water moves sideways through peat and a half-blocked bog drains through its neighbours. Five tenant families hold grazing rights over most of the ground.
intro.mission: Your mission: deliver verified carbon units in three years, on land you do not farm and cannot measure twice.

priorities.label: Measure the baseline while the drained state still exists
Agree terms with the five tenant families who hold the grazing rights
Form a view on which rewetting design the hydrology will support
Lock the buyer's contract and the estate board's mandate

steps.prompt: Put these four actions in the order you would take them, starting with the one you would do first.
steps.why:
Замеры первыми — как в «Harbour Silt Window», но по другой причине, и разница здесь и есть урок. В порту замер шёл первым, потому что от него зависела цена. Здесь замер первым, потому что **окно измерения закрывается навсегда**: перекрытие канав — одна трёхнедельная операция на всё болото, после неё осушённого состояния не остаётся нигде, а год наблюдений с сухим летом внутри нельзя купить, ускорить или повторить.
Два возражения, которые здесь надо разобрать, а не отмахнуться.
**«Нельзя мерить чужую землю, не договорившись с арендаторами — значит S раньше D».** Договориться надо о двух разных вещах, и они несопоставимы по размеру: поставить два десятка дипвеллов на пастбище — это разрешение на страницу, которое даётся за неделю и ничего не меняет в хозяйстве; отдать четыре тысячи гектаров под затопление — это соглашение на тридцать лет. Первое не ждёт второго, а второе без года измерений не о чем вести: пока нет базовой линии, неизвестно, сколько единиц продаётся и сколько семьям причитается.
**«Мандат совета — предусловие: кто-то должен оплатить год измерений».** Верно, и это ровно тот порядок величин, которым мандат не тратится: сеть дипвеллов и год обходов стоят меньше, чем оценка проекта, а капитальное решение принимается через год на измеренных числах. Просить совет о работах до базовой линии — значит просить утвердить цифру, которой пока не существует.

feedback.top: Your order starts the one measurement that cannot be repeated. Everything else on this list can be re-decided next year; the drained state cannot be re-created once the water comes up.
feedback.mid: Your order is workable and it spends part of the only year in which the baseline exists on work that will still be available afterwards.
feedback.low: Your order settles design and contracts first. If the drains go in before a full year of baseline, the units are unverifiable and the whole project is a land improvement with no buyer.

steps.prompt: The estate's peat depth map, on which the whole carbon estimate rests, was digitised from a paper survey drawn in the nineteen-seventies. Where the digitised boundaries can be checked against features still on the ground, they sit up to forty metres out, and not consistently in one direction.

options.text: You probe depth on a fresh grid tied to satellite positioning and use the old map only to decide where the grid needs to be denser.
options.fb: Depth drives the whole carbon estimate, and a forty-metre error that wanders is not a correction you can apply. The old map keeps its one remaining use, which is telling you where the bog is complicated.

options.text: You georeference the old map against the fixed features that can still be identified and probe only where the correction leaves the greatest uncertainty, on the view that a survey walked by people who knew the ground is worth rescuing.
options.fb: Rescuing it is reasonable and the residual error stays unknown exactly where no feature survives, which tends to be the deep middle. You will be probing the edges and estimating the core.

options.text: You apply an average forty-metre buffer to the mapped boundaries and carry the uncertainty into the estimate as a stated margin.
options.fb: The error does not point one way, so an average buffer is a number that describes none of the actual displacements. A stated margin around a meaningless correction is still meaningless.

options.text: You commission an airborne survey of the whole estate, on the view that four thousand hectares of hand probing is a season of work you do not have.
options.fb: It is fast and it measures the surface. Peat depth is the distance to the mineral floor underneath, and that is the number the estimate needs.

steps.prompt: At the first meeting with the five families, the oldest tenant does not object to rewetting. He asks a different question: in ten years, when the bog is wet and the estate is paid for carbon, will it still want graziers on it at all.

options.text: You say that grazing at some level is part of keeping the bog in the condition the credits are sold on, and put that in the agreement as an obligation on the estate rather than a permission to the tenants.
options.fb: He asked whether he is a tenant or a leftover. Writing the grazing into the estate's own obligations answers it with something he can hold, and it happens to be true: wet bog left entirely ungrazed does not stay in the state the buyer paid for.

options.text: You say the estate has no intention of ending the tenancies and that the families have been here longer than anyone on the current board, on the view that a straight assurance from the person in the room is worth more than a clause.
options.fb: Intention is exactly what he is asking about, and intention is what changes when the board does. He wanted the answer in a form that survives you.

options.text: You offer to write a minimum grazing area into the tenancy agreements for the length of the crediting period.
options.fb: A floor in the tenancy is real protection and it is also a minimum, which is the number the estate will move towards. You answered the fear and named the ceiling in the same sentence.

options.text: You say that grazing intensity after rewetting is a question for the hydrologists and will be settled by what the bog can carry.
options.fb: You have referred a question about his family's future to a technical process he has no part in, which is precisely the shape of the thing he was afraid of.

steps.prompt: The baseline year needs a dry summer inside it to be worth anything, and the long-range outlook gives no useful odds either way. Your team can prepare one thing properly before the summer, and the two candidates differ in kind rather than in size.

options.text: You settle the verification standard and its measurement specification first and build the network to it, since a reading taken to no standard is not a reading.
options.fb: A network installed to no specification measures a year to nobody's satisfaction, and six weeks is recoverable inside a twelve-month baseline. You spent the preparation on the thing that decides whether the rest counts.

options.text: You install a provisional network now to whatever specification is most likely, so that nothing is lost if the dry spell comes early, and align it to the standard once chosen.
options.fb: Catching an early dry spell is worth real money and re-aligning a network mid-year means the two halves of the record were taken differently. That is a question the verifier will ask about the summer specifically.

options.text: You install the network to the specification the estate's previous restoration used on the neighbouring lowland bog, since a specification a verifier has already accepted is safer than one still being argued about.
options.fb: That specification was written for lowland raised bog and this site is blanket peat on a slope. The difference is that the provisional route commits to aligning with the standard once it is chosen, while you have adopted a finished answer from somewhere else and will not be checking it again.

B1a.prompt: The network goes in on time and the dry spell arrives. In the third week the two deepest dipwells stop transmitting; the fault is in the loggers and replacements are four weeks away. The keeper is the only person who can reach those wells daily, and he is the same man walking the stock during lambing.

options.text: You pay for relief shepherding for the four weeks and put the keeper on daily manual readings.
options.fb: Manual readings are less precise and they exist, which is the whole difference. Buying the shepherding is what makes the ask possible rather than a favour he will remember.

options.text: You accept the gap and note it in the methodology. Two wells out of a full network is a small proportion.
options.fb: It is a small proportion of the wells and the whole of the dry spell. A verifier reading this will ask precisely about the weeks you cannot show.

options.text: You interpolate the missing weeks from the neighbouring wells once the loggers are back, and document the method.
options.fb: Defensible arithmetic on a normal question and a weak answer on this one: you would be modelling the extreme from the ordinary, which is backwards.

B1b.prompt: The network is in the ground, built to a specification chosen before the standard was. When the standard is settled it turns out to require peat depth at every measurement point to a tolerance the survey was never taken to, and meeting it means walking the whole network again — in the same weeks the summer readings have to be collected.

options.text: You re-probe the points carrying most weight in the estimate first, since the estimate moves with the deep peat, and finish the margins after the summer.
options.fb: Not every point moves the number by the same amount, and the ones that do are a minority. Ordering the re-probing by influence is what makes two jobs fit into one summer.

options.text: You bring in a second team to re-probe everything at once, on the view that a partially compliant network is a network the verifier can reject entirely.
options.fb: Rejection risk is real and a second team walking the same ground as the readings crew is how a dry-spell record acquires disturbance artefacts.

options.text: You record the depths you have as compliant, since the difference falls inside what the tolerance was probably meant to exclude.
options.fb: You have decided what a tolerance was probably meant to exclude, on your own project, about your own data.

steps.prompt: Two rewetting designs reach the same water table. Full drain blocking is cheaper and puts the only vehicle track to the high grazing permanently under water. A bunded causeway costs about a third more and carries the track across the wet ground for the life of the scheme.

options.text: You take the causeway and put the extra cost to the board as the price of the tenants' agreement rather than as an engineering premium.
options.fb: Naming that extra third as relationship cost rather than construction cost is what lets the board judge it correctly. Full blocking would have saved the money and started a thirty-year scheme by cutting five families off from their own hill.

options.text: You take full blocking and offer to fund a new track around the edge of the bog on higher ground.
options.fb: A perimeter track is a real answer and it is a second consent, a second construction season and a longer journey every day for thirty years.

options.text: You take full blocking, on the view that the hydrological outcome is identical and the estate is not obliged to fund a preference.
options.fb: The outcome is identical to the bog and not to the people who cross it, and their agreement is a project input you have already spent months buying.

options.text: You put both designs to the tenants and let them choose, including the cost difference.
options.fb: Handing them the choice is generous and it hands them a cost decision that belongs to the estate. They will choose the one that suits them and you will have agreed to it by default.

steps.prompt: Four of the five families agree terms. The fifth holds ground in the middle of the bog and will not sign; hydrologically, that block cannot be left drained without undermining the whole scheme.

options.text: You ask the four who signed what they think would move him, and let one of them approach him first.
options.fb: The four know things about him that you never will, and an approach from a neighbour is not the same conversation as an approach from the estate. It also tests whether the four are actually with you.

options.text: You raise the offer to him alone until it is accepted, and keep the figure confidential.
options.fb: The figure will not stay confidential in a glen with five farms, and the four who signed first will have learned exactly what signing early is worth.

options.text: You redesign the scheme around his block, accepting a smaller credited area and a weaker hydrological case.
options.fb: A real fallback and an expensive one: you have made one holdout the designer of the project, and the next negotiation starts from that fact.

options.text: You pause the negotiation and go back once the baseline year is complete, since the deadline for works is still two years away.
options.fb: Time genuinely helps here and it is not free: every month he stays outside, the four inside wonder what he is holding out for.

steps.prompt: Nine months into the baseline year, the carbon buyer is acquired. The new owner honours the contract but asks to move delivery forward by a year, offering a fifth more per unit. Doing so means blocking the drains this autumn, three months before the baseline year closes. Two answers are available and they differ in kind.

options.text: You answer on the science: a year earlier means blocking the drains before the baseline year closes, which makes the units unverifiable and worth nothing to either party.
options.fb: The offer is generous and it asks you to end the measurement three months early, which leaves the baseline without the autumn it needs to close. Explaining why their own units would fail verification is the version of no that keeps the contract.

options.text: You answer on the commercial terms: you would need the premium plus the cost of a shortened, weaker baseline priced in, and put a number on it.
options.fb: Treating it as a price question keeps the conversation open and concedes that the baseline is negotiable, which it is not. You may get a number you cannot deliver against.

options.text: You accept in principle and work out afterwards how much of the baseline year can be salvaged. A buyer at this size does not come back a second time to be told no.
options.fb: You have agreed to a date before knowing whether the thing you would deliver on it exists.

B2a.prompt: The baseline year closes. Emissions from the drained bog come out about a third below the figure the project was scoped on. The published figure your scoping used was measured on lowland peat; Ardvane is upland, colder and shallower.

options.text: You re-scope the whole project on the measured figure and take the smaller number to the board with the reason it is smaller.
options.fb: You measured your own bog precisely so that you would not have to use somebody else's. Using it now, including when it disappoints, is the only reason the measurement had value.

options.text: You present both figures and let the board decide which to plan against.
options.fb: One of the two is a measurement of this land and the other is a measurement of different land. That is not a choice, and offering it as one moves your judgement onto people with less information.

options.text: You commission a review of whether the measurement under-reads on shallow upland peat before re-scoping.
options.fb: A fair question that you are asking only because the answer was unwelcome. Had the number come out high, the review would not have been commissioned.

B2b.prompt: The buyer's technical team sends its own proposal: fill the three missing months with a published default emission factor rather than measured data. They cite three projects that did the same — all three on lowland peat, and all three under an earlier version of the standard.

options.text: You put the two mismatches, different peat and a superseded standard, to their team and ask for a precedent that matches on both.
options.fb: Three precedents that match on neither dimension are not three precedents. Asking for one that matches puts the burden where it belongs and does it without calling anybody dishonest.

options.text: You take the assessment to your own verifier and ask whether they would accept it.
options.fb: The verifier's answer is the one that counts and you have skipped a step: you are asking them to referee an argument you have not yet made to the other side.

options.text: You accept the assessment, since their technical team has more carbon-market experience than yours.
options.fb: Their technical team is also paid by the party who wants the earlier date, and the citations they chose are the evidence of that.

steps.prompt: The estate board will approve the works, but wants the tenant payments structured as a share of carbon revenue rather than a fixed sum, so that the estate carries less risk if unit prices fall.

options.text: You propose a floor plus a share: a fixed minimum the families can farm against, with upside if prices hold, because they cannot carry a price they do not set.
options.fb: The board's fear is prices falling and the families' fear is income they cannot plan against. A floor with a share answers both, and neither of them had to lose the argument.

options.text: You accept revenue share. The board is carrying the capital and the families gain from the upside.
options.fb: You have moved the price risk onto five farms with no way to hedge it, in exchange for an upside they cannot borrow against.

options.text: You hold out for fixed payments, since that is what the families were offered and the estate should not renegotiate after agreement.
options.fb: Keeping your word matters and here it forecloses a structure that could have paid them more. The board asked a legitimate question and got a refusal instead of an alternative.

steps.prompt: Whatever shape the grazing terms took, they exist only as words: nothing the families have agreed to is written down and signed. The deed needs their signatures and the estate board's, and the board sits in a month. The machines arrive in three weeks, and preparing the deed takes a week of the same people who are preparing the works.

options.text: You prepare the deed now and get the families' signatures before the machines arrive, leaving the board's to follow.
options.fb: Agreement given in a quiet month is a different thing from agreement asked for while diggers are on the hill. You take the half that decays and leave the half that does not: a board changes its mind less than households watching their grazing disappear.

options.text: You prepare the deed now and hold it unsigned until the board can sign at the same sitting.
options.fb: Tidy, and it keeps both signatures for a month in which only one of them is at risk. The paperwork is right and the sequencing is backwards.

options.text: You put the week into the works and prepare the deed after the board sits.
options.fb: The works are what the week was for, and you will be asking for signatures with the machines already working. Whatever was agreed will not be agreed on the same terms by then.

options.text: You ask the families to confirm the terms by email now and prepare the deed later.
options.fb: An email confirms that they agreed; it does not bind anyone, and it is the form of asking that tells people the agreement was never serious.

steps.prompt: Works begin. In the second week the machines expose a stone structure the regional archaeologist confirms is a shieling, unrecorded and probably eighteenth century. Work in that compartment stops by law. Two routes out, different in kind.

options.text: You bring the archaeologist and the tenants on site, and redesign that compartment around the structure with both of them present.
options.fb: The find belongs to the glen before it belongs to the schedule, and designing around it in the open turns a stoppage into the one part of this project the families will show their children.

options.text: You apply for the consent to record and remove, which the law allows once the structure is documented, and keep the compartment in the scheme.
options.fb: Lawful, funded and quick, and it treats a shieling as an obstacle in a compartment. That is a defensible position you will be defending for the rest of the project.

options.text: You drop the compartment from the scheme entirely and re-cut the boundary around it.
options.fb: Simple and it costs credited area you negotiated for months to assemble, for a structure that could have been designed around rather than excluded.

B3a.prompt: The redesign works and costs three weeks. With the water table already rising in the finished compartments, the verifier asks whether the works were completed to the consented design — and the answer is that one compartment now differs from the drawing the buyer's contract references.

options.text: You disclose the change to the verifier and the buyer before verification starts, since a deviation they find themselves is a different document.
options.fb: A documented deviation disclosed early is a variation; the same deviation found during verification is a question about everything else you did not mention.

options.text: You disclose it to the verifier, since they are the party who signs, and tell the buyer once the units are issued.
options.fb: The verifier will accept it and the buyer will learn that you choose who to tell and when. That is the fact they will carry into the next contract.

options.text: You treat the compartment as within tolerance of the consented design. The hydrological outcome is unchanged.
options.fb: You have made the tolerance judgement yourself, on your own project, on the one point where the drawing and the ground disagree.

B3b.prompt: The compartment is resolved, and the local paper runs a piece on the shieling with a photograph of the machines beside it. Two of the five families are quoted, neither of them warmly. The buyer's new owner reads the trade press, and asks the estate for its account of the week.

options.text: You go to the two families first, before answering the paper, and ask what they would want said.
options.fb: Whatever you say publicly, they will be asked about it in the same shop tomorrow. Letting them shape the answer is the only version where the second article is better than the first.

options.text: You issue a factual statement setting out the consent, the recording work and the archaeologist's involvement.
options.fb: Accurate, complete and addressed to the wrong audience: the buyer will be satisfied and the glen will read it as the estate explaining itself to somebody else.

options.text: You brief the buyer directly and let the local story run its course.
options.fb: You have protected the contract and left the people whose land this is to read about themselves. The buyer's next question will be whether the tenants are with you.

axis.none: замер круга 40: во всём видимом тексте нет ни одного числа с единицей — объявлять нечего. Это не освобождение: класс G краснеет, как только величина заведётся.

title: After the Fire
note: МАКЕТ. Сценарий, тексты и веса — наши. Ни одного числа, имени и формулировки PrepMatter (Ф3). Развилки ветвят по РОДУ хода (Ф21).

intro.head: Welcome to the Sustainable Futures Lab
intro.body: You have joined a small team advising a waste and recycling operator. You will make thirteen decisions. There is one clock for all of them, and you cannot go back.

intro.head: Background
intro.body: Six months ago the sorting hall at the Brackwell materials recovery facility burned for two days. Smoke crossed two residential districts and a primary school was closed for a week. Nobody was hurt and nobody has yet established what was in the smoke. The environmental permit is suspended; the regulator will decide on restart in five months. Two hundred people are on paid stand-by, the town council is split, and the operator has said nothing in public since the week of the fire.
intro.mission: Your mission: get the facility restarting on terms the town can live with, in a town that has heard nothing from the operator for six months.

priorities.label: Go to the two districts before anything is applied for
Establish what actually happened and what was in the smoke
Settle with the regulator what conditions a restart would carry
Form a view on which restart configuration is defensible

steps.prompt: Put these four actions in the order you would take them, starting with the one you would do first.
steps.why:
Стейкхолдеры первыми — как в «Cold Chain Reset», но по другой причине. Там фермы шли первыми, потому что оборудование чужое и без их рук физически ничего не произойдёт. Здесь тратится **доверие, и тратится оно календарём, а не событиями**: неделя молчания стоит одинаково, работает кто-то в это время или нет. Шесть месяцев уже потрачены.
Возражение «нельзя идти к людям, не зная фактов» — ровно та ловушка, из-за которой эти шесть месяцев и прошли: независимая экспертиза дыма идёт четыре месяца, и если ждать её, город решит без тебя. Идти надо с тем, чего не знаешь, назвав это вслух.
**Но экспертиза идёт вторым, а не третьим, и вот почему.** Она длится четыре месяца, регулятор решает через пять — это самый длинный срок в проекте, и он не сжимается ничем. Заказывается она за день, поэтому с разговором в районах не конкурирует: одно делается в первый день недели, другое на второй.
Условия перезапуска идут после неё, потому что вопрос регулятора — «повторится ли», а ответ на него целиком состоит из того, что покажет экспертиза. Конфигурация последней: её незачем проектировать, пока неизвестно, что разрешат и что примет город.

feedback.top: Your order treats six months of silence as the emergency it is, and still starts the four-month investigation in the same week. Neither of them was waiting on the other.
feedback.mid: Your order is defensible and it puts at least one short task ahead of the four-month investigation that gates the regulator's only question.
feedback.low: Your order waits for certainty before speaking and settles conditions before knowing what happened. That is the reasoning that produced six months of silence, and it will produce six more.

steps.prompt: The first public meeting is packed. The first question is not about the fire: a woman asks why nobody from the company came to the school when it reopened.

options.text: You say that nobody came, that there is no good reason why not, and that you are not going to explain it away.
options.fb: She asked a question with no defensible answer, and the only thing that could go wrong was attempting one. Accepting the charge is what buys the right to be heard on everything after it.

options.text: You explain that legal advice at the time restricted what the company could say or do while the investigation was open.
options.fb: You have told a room of parents that lawyers advised the company not to visit their school, which is both true and the worst sentence available.

options.text: You apologise for the omission, set out what the company is doing now, and say when it will next be in the school rather than leaving that open.
options.fb: The apology is right and the pivot is too quick. Moving to what you are doing now is how a room learns that the apology was the part you had to get through.

options.text: You say you were not with the company then and cannot speak to that decision, but can speak to everything from today.
options.fb: Accurate and it separates you from the company you are there to represent. To that room you are the company, and the company has just declined to answer.

steps.prompt: The same meeting asks the question you cannot answer: was the smoke dangerous. The independent air assessment is four months away, and the company's own consultants have an interim view that it probably was not.

options.text: You say the honest answer is that nobody knows yet, name the date the independent work reports, and commit to publishing it whatever it says, because a reassurance you cannot stand behind is spent the day it is contradicted.
options.fb: An honest "we do not know" with a date attached is an answer. Committing to publish before you have seen it is the part that will be remembered when the report arrives.

options.text: You share the consultants' interim view, clearly labelled as preliminary and as the company's own, since a room that has waited six months for any answer deserves the one you actually have.
options.fb: Labelling it does not unmake it: the first number the town hears about its own air will have come from the company that burned, four months before anyone can check it.

options.text: You say you will not speculate ahead of the independent assessment and will come back the week it reports, on the view that a company guessing about its neighbours' health is worse than a company that is slow.
options.fb: Correct discipline, and in a room that has waited six months it sounds like the seventh month starting. Refusing to speculate is not the same as refusing to say anything.

options.text: You offer to fund a second assessment chosen by the council itself, so that the town does not have to take a single report on trust from anybody, including you.
options.fb: Generous and it answers a question about trust with a question about procurement. They asked what was in the smoke, and you offered them a second consultant.

steps.prompt: The regulator will take one substantive submission from you before the decision. You have the team to prepare one of two things properly, and they are different in kind rather than in depth.

options.text: You prepare the cause-and-prevention case: what started the fire, what has changed physically, and what would stop it recurring.
options.fb: The regulator's question is whether it happens again, and everything else in the submission is decoration around that answer. Cause and prevention is the only section they will read twice.

options.text: You prepare the community consent case: what the town has been told, what it asked for, and what the operator has agreed to give it.
options.fb: The regulator does weigh local standing, and it weighs it after it has satisfied itself on recurrence. You have prepared the second question first.

options.text: You prepare the economic case — what the plant employs, what it supplies and what the district loses if it does not reopen — since that is what a decision of this size ultimately weighs.
options.fb: The regulator is not being asked whether the plant is worth having. It is being asked whether it can run without burning again, and a submission about jobs reads as an argument for being allowed to skip that question.

B1a.prompt: The forensic report is inconclusive on ignition, but records eleven overheat alarms on the same conveyor bearing in the year before the fire, all cleared by night-shift staff as false. The report does not link them to the fire.

options.text: You put the eleven alarms in your own submission, before anyone else finds them, and treat the clearing behaviour as the thing to fix.
options.fb: The report did not link them and a hearing will. Bringing them yourself changes the finding from something concealed into the reason your prevention case is credible.

options.text: You follow the forensic conclusion, which is inconclusive, and do not introduce a link the experts declined to draw.
options.fb: You are relying on the experts' caution to avoid mentioning eleven alarms on the bearing that burned, and the log is disclosable.

options.text: You commission a second forensic opinion specifically on the bearing, since the experts declined to draw the link themselves.
options.fb: A reasonable question and it buys weeks to decide whether to disclose something you have already found, which is not how that decision improves.

options.text: You disclose the alarms to the regulator privately and keep them out of the public submission.
options.fb: The regulator gets the truth and the town gets a document with a hole in it, discoverable at the hearing they will attend.

B1b.prompt: A residents' group publishes its own survey: sixty-one per cent of respondents report health effects they attribute to the smoke. The survey was distributed through a campaign mailing list and answered by two hundred and forty people out of eleven thousand households.

options.text: You accept the survey as real evidence of what people experienced, say so, and offer to fund a properly sampled health study alongside it.
options.fb: Attacking the sampling would have been technically correct and politically fatal. Treating it as evidence of experience, and paying for evidence of prevalence, keeps both facts intact.

options.text: You point out the self-selection and the response rate. A figure that unrepresentative will mislead the debate.
options.fb: Every word is defensible statistics and what the town hears is the company that burned explaining why their symptoms do not count.

options.text: You do not comment on the survey and let the independent assessment answer it in due course.
options.fb: Silence has been the company's position for six months, and this is the survey that will fill it in the meantime.

options.text: You meet the residents' group privately to discuss the methodology before responding publicly.
options.fb: The right people and the wrong first sentence: opening with methodology tells them you came to correct the survey rather than to hear it.

steps.prompt: Two restart configurations are open. Full restart brings back all two hundred jobs and the same mixed-waste intake that burned. Partial restart takes clean, pre-sorted material only, employs about ninety, and removes the fire load almost entirely.

options.text: You put partial restart forward as the first stage of a staged return, with the conditions that would have to be met to move to full.
options.fb: Staging is what lets the regulator say yes to something, and naming the conditions in advance is what stops stage two becoming a second fight from zero.

options.text: You seek full restart, on the view that the two hundred jobs are the operator's obligation and that applying for less concedes the site was unsafe before anyone has shown that it was.
options.fb: It did burn for two days over a school. Treating that as a concession to be avoided is how a submission gets refused in full.

options.text: You seek partial restart and say nothing about a later stage, to keep the application as narrow as possible and give the regulator the smallest thing it can say yes to.
options.fb: A clean application, and the day you come back for full intake the town discovers there was always a stage two nobody mentioned.

options.text: You put both options to the regulator and let them specify which they would grant.
options.fb: You have asked the regulator to design your business, and they will choose the one that is easiest to defend rather than the one that works.

steps.prompt: Two hundred people are on stand-by pay, most of them living in the two affected districts. The union asks the company to say publicly that jobs depend on the restart.

options.text: You decline to make that argument publicly and offer instead to fund retraining places for anyone who does not want to return, whatever the decision.
options.fb: Jobs against air quality is an argument that splits families in the same street, and the company would win it by making neighbours choose. Paying for the exit removes the hostage without making the threat.

options.text: You make the argument, since it is true, the workforce has a right to have its position stated, and nobody else in the room is going to say it for them.
options.fb: It is true, and said by the operator it turns two hundred people into leverage: the town hears the plant telling it what its neighbours stand to lose if the answer is no.

options.text: You support the union making the argument itself, without the company making it. The crew speaking for the crew carries a weight no operator statement can buy.
options.fb: Everyone in the town will know who arranged it, and the company will have used its workforce as the voice for the sentence it did not want to be seen saying.

options.text: You commit publicly to the stand-by pay continuing for a fixed further period regardless of the outcome, so that nobody in the two districts is choosing between a wage and an answer.
options.fb: It takes the immediate fear away and it is a promise with an end date, which the workforce will start counting down from the day you make it.

steps.prompt: The independent air assessment reports. It finds no exceedance of any health-based limit, and it also states that the fire brigade's monitors were sited downwind of the plant on the first evening, that the wind veered overnight, and that for thirty-one hours the two districts sat upwind of every instrument. Two ways to carry this, different in kind.

options.text: You publish it whole the day you receive it, with the thirty-one-hour blind spot called out in your own summary, since the gap will be found anyway.
options.fb: The blind spot is the part the town will find, and a report published whole on the day it lands is the only version where you are the one naming it. That is what makes the rest of it believable.

options.text: You publish it whole and, on the same day, announce permanent continuous monitoring so the gap can never recur.
options.fb: Answering a hole in the past with a fix for the future is a real answer and it moves fast past the admission. Some of the room will hear the announcement as the point of the publication.

options.text: You take a week to prepare the communications before publishing, so the gap is properly explained at the moment it appears rather than a fortnight later.
options.fb: A week is long enough for the report to leak and short enough to prove you knew. You would be explaining the delay rather than the gap.

B2a.prompt: A university group re-analyses the published data and reports that modelled concentrations during the thirty-one blind hours, reconstructed from wind records, would have exceeded the short-term limit over the school. Their model has not been peer reviewed.

options.text: You ask the council and the university to name a third party between them to adjudicate the reconstruction, and commit to accepting the finding either way.
options.fb: You cannot judge this and the assessors cannot either — the blind spot is in their own report. Letting the other side help choose the referee, before you know the answer, is what stops this being a search for a verdict.

options.text: You note that the model is not peer reviewed and wait for it to be published properly.
options.fb: Peer review takes months, the school is in the model, and every week of waiting is the company saying the reconstruction is inconvenient rather than wrong.

options.text: You commission your own reconstruction using a different model to test the result.
options.fb: A second model paid for by the operator will be read as the operator's model, and if it disagrees you will have two reconstructions and no resolution.

options.text: You publish the wind records and the raw inputs so anyone can attempt their own reconstruction.
options.fb: Openness is right and it distributes the question rather than answering it. In a month there will be four reconstructions and the school will still not know.

B2b.prompt: Whatever the operator said about the report, the council now asks a question of its own: what would permanent monitoring have shown during the fire. The system the engineers have specified detects combustion products but not the compounds people in the two districts are most afraid of.

options.text: You say so and re-specify the system around what the town is actually afraid of, even though those sensors cost more and need calibration.
options.fb: A monitoring system that measures the wrong thing is worse than none, because it produces reassuring numbers about a question nobody asked. Re-specifying around their fear is what makes it monitoring rather than furniture.

options.text: You explain that the specified sensors follow the regulator's standard for this facility type.
options.fb: The standard was written for routine operation and the town is asking about a two-day fire. Compliance is the answer to a different question than the one asked.

options.text: You add the additional sensors as a second phase once the restart is running.
options.fb: Phase two of a monitoring system is the phase that gets reviewed in a budget round, and the town will know that as well as you do.

steps.prompt: The regulator signals it would grant a partial restart with a condition: an independent monitor on site, funded by the operator, reporting publicly and empowered to halt operations. The operator's owners consider that an unacceptable transfer of control.

options.text: You take the condition to the owners as the price of operating at all here, with the alternative, no permit, stated in the same paper.
options.fb: The choice is not between control and less control, it is between less control and no site. Putting both on one page is what stops the owners answering a question that was never on the table.

options.text: You negotiate the halt power down to a recommendation the operator must respond to within a fixed time, on the view that an outside party able to stop a plant on its own judgement is not something any owner will sign.
options.fb: A monitor who can recommend is a consultant, and the town will read the change correctly the first time there is an incident to recommend about.

options.text: You accept the condition and inform the owners afterwards, since the alternative is no restart and a decision that has only one survivable outcome is not a decision to put up for debate.
options.fb: The judgement is right and it was not yours to make. A mandate spent without asking is a mandate you do not have next time.

options.text: You propose that the monitor be jointly appointed by the council and the regulator, so that the operator is not in the position of funding and selecting its own supervisor.
options.fb: Joint appointment strengthens the monitor's standing and it also puts a second body in the approval path, which is weeks you are spending to make a condition you were going to accept more palatable.

steps.prompt: Restart is granted for eight weeks' time. Suppression commissioning, crew recruitment and training, the monitoring with its public feed, and the reopening communications all have owners and all will be delivered. Three of the four are working to a scope signed off weeks ago. The monitoring is not: what the operator has to build to satisfy the condition settled with the regulator is still being written. You can carry one of them yourself; the rest go to people who are competent and who will not bring small decisions back to you.

options.text: The monitoring build on our side of it: sensors, calibration and what goes out to the feed, since that scope is the one still open.
options.fb: It is the only one of the four where the work is still being defined, and it is the half of the restart the town was promised in public. A reasonable-looking narrowing — a cheaper sensor, a feed switched on a week after opening — is not a schedule slipping; it is the promise quietly becoming smaller, inside a specification nobody outside will read until it matters.

options.text: The suppression commissioning, because a second fire ends the site and everything else with it.
options.fb: The stakes are the largest and the work is the most specified: a signed-off scope and an accountable contractor do not need you in the room. You went where the consequence is rather than where the judgement is left.

options.text: The reopening communications, since you are the person the two districts have been dealing with for four months.
options.fb: Defensible, and it is the item where you are hardest to replace: you have been answering to the town's face since the first meeting. What it costs is the one scope still open — communications reports what the other three did, and by the time you are describing the monitoring it is built.

options.text: The crew recruitment and training. The people coming back have to trust the person asking them to.
options.fb: They do, and they will not learn it from you in a classroom. A shift supervisor who was here that night rebuilds a crew better than a manager who was not, and eight weeks of your attention there buys the restart nothing it does not already have.

steps.prompt: Four days before reopening, the council's waste department points out that its own contract with the operator requires the plant to accept municipal mixed collections from the day it opens. The partial-restart permit allows pre-sorted material only. Two ways out, different in kind.

options.text: You go to the council to vary the waste contract to pre-sorted for the permit's first stage, and offer to carry the cost of the extra sorting they will have to do.
options.fb: Two contracts that contradict each other are a problem for whoever holds both, and that is you. Paying for the sorting is what turns a demand on the council into an offer they can take to their own committee.

options.text: You open on pre-sorted only and take the contractual breach, on the view that the permit is the binding instrument and a commercial penalty is the cheaper of the two failures.
options.fb: The permit does bind harder, and you have chosen to be in default with the one party whose committee decides whether you are welcome here. Cheaper is not the same as survivable.

options.text: You accept the municipal collections and sort them on site before processing, since the material is pre-sorted by the time it enters the hall.
options.fb: The permit restricts what comes through the gate, not what reaches the hall, and you have decided otherwise on your own reading four days before opening.

B3a.prompt: The variation is agreed and the plant opens on pre-sorted material. In the first month the monitor's public feed shows three short spikes on the new sensors, all well below any limit and all matching scheduled intake. The council asks whether spikes will be explained each time.

options.text: You commit to a standing explanation alongside every spike, published by the monitor rather than by the operator.
options.fb: An unexplained number on a public feed is worse than no feed, because the town fills the silence. Routing the explanation through the monitor is what stops it reading as the operator's commentary on its own data.

options.text: You commit to explaining any spike that exceeds a threshold agreed in advance with the monitor, so that the feed carries commentary where it matters rather than everywhere.
options.fb: A threshold is sensible and it puts you back in the position of deciding which readings deserve an explanation, which is the position this whole year was spent getting out of.

options.text: You point out that all three are within limits and that routine commentary would imply they matter.
options.fb: They are within limits and they matter to the people watching the feed, which is the entire population the feed was built for.

B3b.prompt: The plant opens in breach of the waste contract. Within a fortnight the council's legal officer writes asking the operator to confirm whether it intends to perform the contract at all, copying the committee that will review the permit conditions in six months.

options.text: You answer that the operator cannot perform under this permit, propose the variation, and say the timing was your error, since the committee will read this.
options.fb: The letter asks whether you are a counterparty or a problem. The only answer that survives the committee reading it in six months is the one that names the mistake and arrives with the fix attached.

options.text: You answer that performance is suspended by regulatory impossibility and reserve the operator's position, on the view that a legal letter deserves a legal reply.
options.fb: It is the correct reply to a lawyer and the wrong reply to a committee, and the committee is the audience the letter was copied to.

options.text: You ask for a meeting with the waste department before replying in writing, so that the reply can be agreed rather than served.
options.fb: Agreeing the reply beats serving one, and the letter has a date on it. Two weeks of arranging a meeting is two weeks of an unanswered legal letter sitting in the committee's papers.
