options.fb: It saves less than the maltings and spends the goodwill of nine hundred owners in the month they most notice.

options.text: You do nothing differently this summer and take the draw as it comes.
options.fb: Which is precisely how a company arrives at a threshold without a single decision on record that took it there.
leads: сухое лето прошло по своему решению

B1a.prompt: Word gets round that the company is planning to take from storage this summer. A retired engineer who reads every board paper writes to ask what the plan is for putting it back, and copies in forty households.

options.text: You answer him with the volume, the year it comes back and what has to be true for that to hold.
options.fb: He asked the one question the last four years never had an answer to. Giving him the year it comes back is what makes the answer something you can be held to.

options.text: You reply that storage exists precisely for dry summers and that this is what it is for.
options.fb: True, and it is the sentence under which two hundred megalitres left the bank without a decision anyone can now point to.

options.text: You invite him to see the leak programme's first zone and the figures behind it.
options.fb: Generous and it answers a question he did not ask. The zone is the answer to next year; he asked about this summer.

needs: сухое лето прошло по своему решению

B1b.prompt: Asking anyone to use less makes the company the arbiter of who gives up what, and the valley knows within the week which way it went. The maltings manager rings: he wants to know how a company owned by nine hundred households decides between their hosepipes and his sixty jobs.

options.text: You put the two options side by side with what each saves and ask him which he would defend.
options.fb: He is right that he was asked first, and the comparison is the only thing that turns being singled out into being consulted.

options.text: You explain that his 1.1 megalitres is the largest single tap and that the arithmetic points at it.
options.fb: The arithmetic does point at it, which he already knows. Stated alone it says the company solves problems where they are easiest to solve.

options.text: You put both options back to the board priced side by side, rather than defending the one already taken.
options.fb: Honest and late: the decision has been made and announced, and reopening it costs you the standing to make the next one.

steps.prompt: The 900-megalitre buffer figure comes from a 1998 study of the whole chalk block. The company's own monitoring covers one borehole. The 200 already drawn is an arithmetic residual — abstraction minus recharge, summed over four years — not a measurement of anything.

options.text: You have recharge rebuilt from the four wettest and four driest of the last ten years.
options.fb: The residual is only as good as the recharge it subtracts, and a ten-year average hides the two years that decide a dry decade. Rebuild the divisor before arguing about the total.

options.text: You commission a new study of the whole chalk block.
options.fb: It will be better than the 1998 one and arrive in about eighteen months, which is half of what is left.

options.text: You drill two more monitoring boreholes to see whether the one you have is representative.
options.fb: Worth doing for the next decade. It tells you about the shape of the aquifer, not about the number in every board paper.

options.text: You keep the 900 and the 200, since both have been used consistently for four years.
options.fb: Consistency is not accuracy. A figure repeated in eight board papers is still one study from 1998.

steps.prompt: The rebuilt recharge figure comes back at 3.7 rather than 4.0 megalitres a day. The deficit is 0.9, not 0.6, and the buffer runs out sooner than the leak programme finishes. The programme still saves 0.7.

options.text: You keep the programme and find the remaining 0.2 in the interim, naming where each part comes from.
options.fb: The programme was never going to be enough on the new number and remains the only permanent part. What changes is that the bridge now needs a name and a size.

options.text: You take the whole gap to the maltings, whose 1.1 is more than twice what is missing.
options.fb: It closes the arithmetic in one call and puts the entire adjustment on sixty jobs, none of whom have seen the new recharge figure.

options.text: You accelerate the leak programme with a second contractor to finish inside two years, paying the premium out of the interim savings.
options.fb: Money can buy some of that time and not all of it: the second contractor works the same streets and the same shut-off windows.

options.text: You hold the old 4.0 in the plan until a second study confirms 3.7.
options.fb: The company would then be planning against the number it prefers, in the year the difference stops being theoretical.

steps.prompt: Two bridges over the remaining gap. The neighbouring town's utility will sell 0.3 megalitres a day on a three-year contract at a price that takes a fifth of the company's margin. Or the company can hold the gap itself by running the buffer lower and accepting that the gauge may fail in one August out of three.

options.text: You buy the water for the three years the programme needs and say why in the board paper.
options.fb: A fifth of margin for three years is expensive and finite. An August that fails is a quarter of the licence for ever, and no amount of margin buys it back.

options.text: You hold the gap yourselves and tell the regulator the company is running the buffer down deliberately, with the date it stops.
options.fb: Declared, it is a plan rather than a drift, and it still rests on three Augusts behaving.

options.text: You buy a smaller volume and hold part of the gap, splitting the risk between price and August.
options.fb: Splitting a risk that is not linear: the August that fails costs the same whether you were half exposed or fully.

options.text: You hold the gap and say nothing to the regulator until the programme is finished.
options.fb: The borehole readings go to them quarterly. They will see the drawdown and read the silence beside it.

B2a.prompt: Buying water means a bill the households own. The neighbouring utility's engineer mentions, informally, that two other small companies on the same chalk are in the same position and that none of them has ever bought together.

options.text: You propose a joint purchase on one shared term, keeping your own volume and dates inside it.
options.fb: Three buyers on one term is a better price and a slower signature. Keeping your own volume inside the deal is what stops the price gain costing you the dates.

options.text: You buy alone at the offered price, since three timetables will not fit inside yours.
options.fb: The timetable risk is real and you have paid for it in a price the households will see printed.

options.text: You propose a joint approach covering purchase, monitoring and future licence terms.
options.fb: Everything on the table means nothing signed before the dry season. The wider the ask, the later the answer.

B2b.prompt: Running the buffer down deliberately puts a number in the public quarterly return that anyone can read. The angling association that fishes the chalk stream reads it first and asks to meet before it writes to the regulator.

options.text: You meet them, show the drawdown, the date it stops and what the programme delivers by then.
options.fb: They are going to write either way. The letter written after seeing an end date is a different letter from the one written after being refused a meeting.

options.text: You tell them the drawdown is within licence and that the regulator has been informed.
options.fb: Both true and neither is what they asked. They came to find out whether the stream has a future, and heard about paperwork.

options.text: You offer them a seat on the company's monitoring review for the three years.
options.fb: Generous and it commits you to three years of meetings with people who have not yet been told what the drawdown ends at.

steps.prompt: The leak programme has three kinds of zone: the old town centre, where losses are highest and the streets are narrowest; the post-war estates, where the pipe is uniform and the work is fast; and the outlying farms, where the pipe is longest and the customers fewest. The contractor can only be in one kind of zone at a time.

options.text: You do the estates first: uniform pipe returns megalitres per month sooner than the centre.
options.fb: The measure is not where the water is lost, it is how fast the loss can be stopped. On a three-year clock the fast zones are worth more than the leaky ones.

options.text: You start in the town centre, where the losses are largest.
options.fb: The biggest prize and the slowest streets. It is the right answer on a five-year programme and the wrong one on this clock.

options.text: You alternate between the centre and the estates so that neither trade goes idle.
options.fb: Two mobilisations instead of one, and a monthly saving curve that flattens exactly when the board is watching it.

options.text: You start with the farms, where the pipe runs longest per customer.
options.fb: Most pipe, fewest customers, and the smallest share of the loss you are trying to stop this year.

steps.prompt: At the annual meeting a household asks why the bill is rising when the reservoir on the hill is visibly full. The reservoir holds two days of supply and is filled from the aquifer; it has nothing to do with what is left underground. Two hundred owners are in the room and most of them have looked at that reservoir their whole lives.

options.text: You explain what the reservoir is for, that it is filled from what is running down, and what the bill buys.
options.fb: The full reservoir is the strongest argument in the room and it is about the wrong thing. Explaining what it is for turns their own evidence into yours.

options.text: You put up the borehole chart and take the room through four years of drawdown line by line.
options.fb: The right data and the wrong starting point: the chart argues with what they can see out of the window rather than explaining it.

options.text: You say the reservoir is not relevant to the question and move on to the programme.
options.fb: It is relevant to two hundred people who can see it, and telling them otherwise ends the meeting's willingness to hear the rest.

options.text: You offer to take anyone who wants to the borehole to see the measurement taken.
options.fb: Six people will come and two hundred will leave with the reservoir still full in their minds.

steps.prompt: Two years in, the leak work is ahead of schedule and the bought 0.3 is still flowing, so today the company sits about 0.3 to the good — for as long as the contract lasts. The maltings asks for an extra 0.3 megalitres a day to add a line and thirty jobs. On today's numbers the company can supply it. On the ten-year recharge it cannot.

options.text: You offer the volume against a rule holding total abstraction below recharge.
options.fb: The company is being asked to spend the surplus it has just built. A rule that ties new demand to new savings is what stops the next four years repeating the last four.
leads: солодовне отказано или дано под правило

options.text: You supply the 0.3 now and review the position each year against the borehole.
options.fb: Reviewed annually by the same board that wants the jobs. That is how the first 260 megalitres left.

options.text: You refuse until the programme is complete and the new recharge study is in.
options.fb: Defensible and it costs thirty jobs a decision that could have been shaped rather than declined.
leads: солодовне отказано или дано под правило

options.text: You supply it from the bought water rather than the aquifer, and pass the price through to the maltings.
options.fb: It solves this year at a price nobody will pay in year four, when the contract ends and the line still needs the water.

B3a.prompt: The maltings did not get its extra volume, and the first year afterwards looks wrong: the borehole level rises 0.3 metres, far more than the balance can explain. The hydrogeologist says one wet winter, the contractor says the leak work, and the maltings has quietly been running below its allocation all year.

options.text: You separate the three by what each would have to be worth, and report a range rather than a cause.
options.fb: Three explanations for one rise, and the company is about to write one of them into next year's plan. A range with three named contributions survives the second wet winter that does not come.

options.text: You credit the leak programme, since it is the one thing the company controls and paid for.
options.fb: The most convenient cause, chosen in the year the board is deciding whether to fund the rest of it.

options.text: You wait for a second year before attributing anything.
options.fb: Right instinct and one year of not knowing, in a company that is about to set next year's allocation on this number.

needs: солодовне отказано или дано под правило

B3b.prompt: The line is running. The quarterly return now carries two numbers pointing opposite ways: the borehole level is rising after a wet winter, and the volume leaving the works is the highest in six years. The regulator's officer asks which of the two the company manages against.

options.text: You answer that the company manages against the balance, show both numbers, and say which one would make you stop.
options.fb: He asked which number governs. Naming the level at which you would stop is the only answer that distinguishes a policy from an explanation.

options.text: You point to the rising buffer, which is the outcome that matters.
options.fb: It is rising because of a winter nobody arranged, and the officer can read a rainfall record as easily as you can.

options.text: You undertake to bring abstraction back under recharge within twelve months.
options.fb: A real commitment made on the spot, without the board that would have to fund the last 0.2 of it.

title: Paid to Fail
note: МАКЕТ. Тексты и веса наши, ни одной формулировки PrepMatter (Ф3). Развилки по РОДУ хода (Ф21). Связывающее — УСПЕХ, КОТОРЫЙ ЛОМАЕТ МЕХАНИЗМ: компании платят за тонну, отведённую от полигона; она отвела столько, что тонн стало меньше, и доход падает ровно потому, что работа сделана. Разобрать надо то, что тебя кормит. Против десяти: 01 данные · 02 календарь · 03 окно · 04 чужие активы · 05 необратимость · 06 доверие · 07 деньги с датой · 08 очередь · 09 два правила · 10 ресурс во времени. Ключ A>D>S>H: рычаг один и он контрактный — среднесрочный пересмотр бывает единожды.

intro.head: Welcome to the Sustainable Futures Lab
intro.body: You have joined a small team advising a council-owned recycling company. You will make thirteen decisions. There is one clock for all of them, and you cannot go back.

intro.head: Background
intro.body: Marden Resource Recovery is paid £62 a tonne for every tonne it keeps out of landfill, under a ten-year contract with the council of which four years have gone. It diverted 41,000 tonnes last year — £2.54m against fixed costs of £2.1m — and it did its job so well that the town now throws away less every year. Total waste is falling about 9 per cent a year as reuse and repair spread, and the company's income falls with it. The contract has one mid-term review, and it opens in seven months. Sixty people work here.
intro.mission: Your mission: keep the company alive on the strength of the very thing that is closing it.

priorities.label: Get the council to reopen how the company is paid, at the one review it has
Establish how fast the tonnage really falls and what it does to the surplus
Tell sixty people what is happening before the figures reach them another way
Work out what the company could be paid for instead of tonnes

steps.prompt: Put these four actions in the order you would take them, starting with the one you would do first.
steps.why:
Связывающее — **успех, который ломает механизм**. Компанию платят за тонну, отведённую от полигона; она отводит так хорошо, что тонн становится меньше, и доход падает **ровно потому, что работа сделана**. Это новая семья: в «The Spend-By Date» деньги сгорали по календарю, здесь они тают от собственного результата.
Совет первым — и не потому, что он главный, а потому что **у рычага одна дата**. Среднесрочный пересмотр открывается через семь месяцев и бывает единожды за десять лет; пропустить его — значит шесть лет жить по формуле, которая наказывает за работу. Всё остальное можно сделать позже, эту дверь позже открыть нельзя.
Возражение сильное: **идти к плательщику без числа — получить отписку**, и наша же библиотека учит сначала мерить. Верно наполовину. К пересмотру идут не с числом, а с **заявкой на пересмотр**: она процедурная, подаётся заранее и стоит письма. Число нужно к слушанию, а не к заявке, и оно вторым.
Данные вторыми: падение тонн и падение излишка — разные скорости, и от их разницы зависит, о чём просить. Люди третьими: шестьдесят человек узнают из городской газеты, если мы будем ждать готового ответа. Новая формула последней — и возражение к этому сильнее прочих: **как просить пересмотр, не зная, за что хочешь получать**. Отвечаю: к слушанию форма нужна, и к шагам 4 и 7 она появится. Но написанная до заявки, она превращает пересмотр в защиту своей конструкции; написанная после — остаётся предметом торга, каким и должна быть.

feedback.top: You file for the review first because it opens once in ten years, and bring the number to the hearing rather than to the letter.
feedback.mid: Workable. The review is not last, and the company will reach the hearing with something to say.
feedback.low: This order designs a new payment mechanism before asking whether the payer will hear one, and the door that matters opens once.

steps.prompt: The review has to be requested in writing, and the clerk says requests are usually made by the council, not by the contractor. Nothing in the contract says the contractor cannot ask. The window opens in seven months and closes six weeks later.

options.text: You file the request now in plain terms and say the case will follow.
options.fb: Filing is procedural and costs a letter; the case is an argument and costs three months. Doing them in that order is what keeps both.

options.text: You ask the clerk what a contractor's request has to contain before you send anything.
options.fb: Careful and it spends two weeks discovering that the answer is «a request». The form here is thinner than the fear of it.

options.text: You wait until the surplus figures for the year are audited, so the request lands with evidence behind it.
options.fb: Evidence belongs at the hearing. The audit lands two months after the window closes.

options.text: You raise it informally with the cabinet member and let her decide whether to open the review.
options.fb: She may well open it, and you have made the one dated lever in the contract depend on somebody remembering a conversation.

steps.prompt: Tonnage collected is down 12 per cent on last year while the town's total waste fell about 9. The finance officer reads the 12 as the trend. Two of the four rounds changed to fortnightly collection in the same year, and a large employer closed in the spring.

options.text: You separate the fall into what the town stopped throwing away and what left the town.
options.fb: One of the two is your success and the other is somebody's redundancy. Asking the council to change a formula means knowing which is which.

options.text: You take the 9 per cent as it stands, since it is the number the council will use anyway.
options.fb: They will use it, and at the hearing you will be arguing about a number you have not taken apart.

options.text: You model three scenarios from 5 to 12 per cent and present the range.
options.fb: A range is honest and it postpones the question the range exists to answer: which part of the fall is permanent.

options.text: You commission a waste-composition study of the whole district.
options.fb: Nine months and a large invoice for a question your own weighbridge tickets can answer by round.

steps.prompt: Two ways to be paid for something other than tonnes. A payment for outcomes the council actually wants — waste avoided, materials kept in use — which nobody in the county has yet written into a contract. Or a floor under the existing rate, which is familiar, quick, and leaves the perverse formula intact.

options.text: You put the floor and the outcome payment into a single paper, one as the ask and one as the direction.
options.fb: The floor is what the council can grant in six weeks; the direction is what stops you being here again in year eight. One paper keeps them from being traded against each other.
leads: в бумаге и пол, и механизм

options.text: You put the outcome payment alone, since a floor rewards the same wrong thing more gently and buys six quiet years.
options.fb: Right about the formula and it asks a council with six weeks to invent a contract type the county has never used.

options.text: You ask only for the floor and leave the mechanism for the next contract.
options.fb: It buys six years of the same perverse formula, and the next contract is negotiated by whoever is here then.

options.text: You ask for the contract to be terminated early and retendered on a new basis.
options.fb: Termination is the one door that cannot be reopened, offered to a council that has not yet been asked for the cheap thing.

B1a.prompt: The finance officer reads the paper and picks up the floor immediately: it is a number she can put in a budget line. She has not mentioned the second half, and the hearing is in five weeks.

options.text: You thank her for the floor and ask what would have to be true for the second half to be piloted on one round.
options.fb: She took what she could use. A pilot on one round is the smallest version of the second half that still exists after the hearing.

options.text: You press for both together, since separating them is how the direction gets lost between one budget round and the next.
options.fb: Pressing a person who has just said yes to something is how the yes gets reopened.

options.text: You accept the floor and put the outcome payment into the next contract's brief.
options.fb: Clean and it moves the argument to a document nobody has started, to be read by people not yet appointed.

needs: в бумаге и пол, и механизм

B1b.prompt: By the end of the week two versions of the paper are circulating at the depot, and neither of them is the paper. One says the contract is being torn up; the other says the tonnage bonus is going.

options.text: You tell the depot in one sentence what the paper actually asks for.
options.fb: Rumour beats you to the floor whenever the true account is longer than the false one. One sentence travels; a briefing does not.

options.text: You call an all-staff meeting for the following week and set out the whole position.
options.fb: The right meeting, seven days after the week in which people decide what they believe.

options.text: You say nothing until the council answers, since half the versions will be wrong either way.
options.fb: Both versions are already moving, and silence is read as confirmation of whichever one frightens people more.

steps.prompt: The company's case rests on a claim that reuse is displacing waste. The evidence is the town's two repair cafés and a furniture reuse shop, whose own records count items rather than tonnes, and count them at the point of donation.

options.text: You weigh a sample of their items instead of assuming an average weight.
options.fb: A sofa and a toaster are one item each. The council will test this number harder than any other in the paper, because it is the one that asks them for money.

options.text: You use published average weights per item category.
options.fb: Defensible and borrowed. The first question at the hearing will be whether those averages are from a town like this one.

options.text: You drop the reuse claim and argue on tonnage alone.
options.fb: It is the strongest part of the story and the hardest to prove, and dropping it leaves you arguing that success looks like decline.

options.text: You ask the reuse shop to start recording weights from next month, so that next year's case rests on measurement.
options.fb: Good for next year's case. The hearing is in five weeks.

steps.prompt: The floor can be set two ways. At the current £2.54m, which freezes today's income for six years and asks the council for the most. Or at fixed costs plus a margin — £2.3m — which is defensible line by line and gives up £240,000 of a surplus that is £440,000.

options.text: You ask for the defensible figure with the working shown, and name what the difference buys.
options.fb: A number the council can defend in public survives its own finance committee. Naming what the difference buys is what stops it being read as a discount.

options.text: You ask for the current income and let them negotiate down.
options.fb: Standard practice and it invites the committee to find its own number, which will be below both of yours.

options.text: You ask for costs plus a margin and say the pilot will be funded separately.
options.fb: Two asks in two papers, the second of which arrives after the review window has closed.

options.text: You ask for a floor indexed to the town's total waste, so it falls more slowly than income.
options.fb: An index tied to the very thing you are trying to reduce, explained to a committee in six weeks.

steps.prompt: A week before the hearing the council's waste officer says privately that the cabinet will not grant a floor in an election year, but might fund a pilot. The floor is the part that keeps sixty people employed; the pilot is the part that changes the formula.

options.text: You go into the hearing with both and let the cabinet choose in public which one it is refusing.
options.fb: A refusal made in the room is a decision with a name on it. Withdrawing the floor in advance saves them from ever making it.
leads: на слушание идут с обоими требованиями

options.text: You drop the floor and ask only for the pilot, taking the officer's read as good and saving the cabinet a public refusal.
options.fb: His read is probably right, and you have conceded the employment case to a corridor conversation with no author.
leads: одно из двух требований снято до слушания

options.text: You ask for the floor alone and hold the pilot for a calmer year.
options.fb: It protects the sixty and leaves the formula intact for the six years in which it does its damage.
leads: одно из двух требований снято до слушания

options.text: You ask the officer to put his read in writing before you decide anything.
options.fb: He will decline, politely, and the week you spent asking was the week to rewrite the paper.
leads: на слушание идут с обоими требованиями

B2a.prompt: The hearing is public and three of the town's repair and reuse groups have asked whether they should attend. They are the evidence for half the case and they have never spoken at a council committee.

options.text: You invite them and ask each for one specific thing they have seen, rather than support for the company.
options.fb: A committee discounts an ally speaking for a contractor and cannot discount a resident describing a Saturday. The narrower the testimony, the harder it is to wave away.

options.text: You invite them and brief them on the company's argument so the messages align.
options.fb: Aligned messages read as coached, and the one thing they have that you do not is that nobody pays them.

options.text: You thank them and keep the hearing to the company, to avoid the appearance of a lobby.
options.fb: Defensible, and it keeps out of the room the only voices whose interest is not financial.

needs: на слушание идут с обоими требованиями

B2b.prompt: Whatever went in, the paper is now narrower than what the depot was told. The shop steward asks, in front of the shift, whether the sixty jobs are in the paper at all.

options.text: You say what is in the paper and what is not, and why the second was left out.
options.fb: He asked a question with a yes-or-no shape and a real answer behind it. Giving the reason is what stops the answer becoming the rumour.

options.text: You say the jobs are safe while the contract runs, which is true for six years.
options.fb: True, and it answers a question about the paper with a fact about the contract, in front of people who can tell the difference.

options.text: You promise to take the jobs question back to the board before the hearing.
options.fb: A real commitment made to buy the end of a difficult conversation, with five days to keep it.

needs: одно из двух требований снято до слушания

steps.prompt: If the pilot is funded, it can start on one of three rounds. The town centre has the most reuse and the worst data. The estates have the best data and the least reuse. The villages have neither, and the councillor who chairs the committee lives there.

options.text: You start on the estates, where a small effect can be measured and defended.
options.fb: A pilot exists to produce a number the committee will believe. Good data on a small effect beats a large effect nobody can size.

options.text: You start in the town centre, where the effect will be largest and the story easiest to tell to a committee.
options.fb: The biggest effect and the weakest measurement, presented to the people who fund year two.

options.text: You start in the villages, since the chair will see it working.
options.fb: It buys one councillor's attention and spends the pilot on the round least likely to show anything.

options.text: You run a light version across all three to avoid choosing.
options.fb: Three thin datasets, none of which settles the question the pilot was funded to settle.

steps.prompt: At the depot briefing a driver of eleven years says the quiet part aloud: if the town throws away less every year, what is he for? Forty people are in the canteen and the answer «the pilot» means nothing to any of them.

options.text: You answer that the work changes shape rather than disappears, and describe the first changed round.
options.fb: He asked what he is for. The only answer that lands in a canteen is a description of a Tuesday, not a description of a strategy.

options.text: You say the floor protects every job for six years and leave the question of what comes after it for later.
options.fb: It answers the fear and confirms the thing he said: that after six years there is nothing.

options.text: You admit you do not yet know and promise to come back with the answer.
options.fb: Honest, and it leaves forty people holding the question. Worth saying only if you come back with the answer inside the week.

options.text: You put the question to the room and ask what they think the work becomes.
options.fb: They came to be told something. Asked instead, they hear that management has no answer either.

steps.prompt: The cabinet grants the pilot and half the floor, on condition the company publishes its diversion and reuse figures every quarter. Published quarterly, a bad quarter is a headline. The finance officer suggests the condition can be softened to annual if asked now.

options.text: You accept quarterly and publish the method alongside the first set.
options.fb: The condition is the price of the argument you just won: you asked to be judged on outcomes. Publishing the method is what makes a bad quarter a question rather than a verdict.

options.text: You ask for annual, since a quarterly headline can end the pilot in month four.
options.fb: A real risk, and asking to be measured less often in the week you argued for being measured differently.

options.text: You accept quarterly and publish only the figures the condition names.
options.fb: Compliant and bare. The first bad quarter arrives with nothing beside it.

options.text: You accept and ask that the first two quarters be treated as a baseline.
options.fb: Reasonable and it reads as arranging the scoreboard before the game.

B3a.prompt: The first published quarter is bad: diversion down, reuse flat, and the local paper runs it under the company's own name. The cause is visible in your own data — the estates round was suspended for three weeks by a depot fire — and the correction is dull.

options.text: You publish the three-week gap and the corrected series in the same week.
options.fb: A dull correction published early is a footnote. The same correction published after the second story is a defence.

options.text: You write to the paper asking for a correction.
options.fb: The paper reported the number you published. The argument is with your own presentation of it.

options.text: You wait for the next quarter, which will show the recovery on its own.
options.fb: It will, three months after the committee has formed its view of the pilot.

B3b.prompt: The pilot now runs under a measurement regime the company itself asked to soften. Halfway through the year the reuse figures are strong, and nobody outside the company has seen them.

options.text: You publish the half-year figures voluntarily, with the method, ahead of the requirement.
options.fb: You asked for the measurement to be softened and got it; going first with a good number is what turns that into trust rather than into suspicion at year end.

options.text: You hold to the annual cycle you asked for, and report in full at the year with the method beside it.
options.fb: Consistent with what you asked for, and it leaves a year in which the committee hears about the pilot only from people who doubt it.

options.text: You brief the chair privately on the strong figures.
options.fb: One councillor knows and the record shows nothing, which is the arrangement that looks worst if it is ever described.

title: The Only One Who Knows
note: МАКЕТ. Тексты и веса наши, ни одной формулировки PrepMatter (Ф3). Развилки по РОДУ хода (Ф21). Связывающее — ЗНАНИЕ, ЖИВУЩЕЕ В ОДНОМ ЧЕЛОВЕКЕ: ограничение не деньги, не срок и не правило, а человек, который уходит, и то, чего он никогда не записывал. Против одиннадцати семей. Ключ H>S>D>A: сначала объявляется, ЧТО именно надо снять, иначе разговор с ним превращается в уговоры остаться.

intro.head: Welcome to the Sustainable Futures Lab
intro.body: You have joined a small team advising a municipal heat and water utility. You will make thirteen decisions. There is one clock for all of them, and you cannot go back.

intro.head: Background
intro.body: Everything at Kelder Works is controlled by a system built in 1974 and extended ever since: 320 control loops, of which eleven are documented. One engineer understands the rest. He retires in five months, after forty years, and has never been asked to write any of it down. A mandated cyber upgrade has to be finished in fourteen months and cannot be specified until the logic is mapped. The vendor will reverse-engineer the system for £480,000 in nine months. There are three junior engineers.
intro.mission: Your mission: still be able to run the works the week after he leaves.

priorities.label: Decide which of the 320 loops actually have to be captured before he goes
Ask him, in a way that does not read as a request to stay
Find out what documentation already exists, in whatever form
Tell the regulator what the upgrade timetable now depends on

steps.prompt: Put these four actions in the order you would take them, starting with the one you would do first.
steps.why:
Связывающее — **знание, живущее в одном человеке**. Не деньги, не срок и не правило: ограничение — человек, который уходит через пять месяцев, и триста двадцать контуров, из которых записаны одиннадцать. Новая семья: в «Cold Chain Reset» рычага не было над чужими активами, здесь рычага нет над чужой головой, и она уходит по календарю.
Первым — не он, а **список**. Снять за пять месяцев всё невозможно, и разговор, начинающийся без списка, неизбежно превращается в уговоры остаться: человеку нечего предъявить, кроме собственной незаменимости. Список меняет предмет разговора с «останься» на «вот двадцать два контура, без которых площадка не запустится, — расскажи про них».
Возражение сильное: **список без него и составить нельзя**, ведь никто, кроме него, не знает, что важно. Верно про полноту и неверно про порядок. Двадцать с небольшим критических контуров видны с площадки: это те, чей отказ останавливает подачу. Грубый список, составленный за два дня своими силами, он **исправит за час** — а вот пустой лист он будет заполнять полгода, и заполнит не тем.
Он вторым: пока он здесь, всё остальное подождёт. Существующие бумаги третьими — их ценность известна только после того, как ясно, что ищем. Регулятор последним: ему нужен не факт ухода, а новая дата, а даты до третьего шага не существует.

feedback.top: You bring him a list rather than a blank sheet, which is what keeps the conversation about the works instead of about him.
feedback.mid: Workable: he is not last, and the utility will get something written down while he is still here.
feedback.low: This order goes to the regulator or the archive before deciding what has to be captured, and the man with the knowledge leaves on a fixed date.

steps.prompt: Nobody can capture 320 loops in five months. The plant manager wants the list drawn up by criticality; the vendor's method starts from the network diagram and works inwards; the three juniors between them have touched about forty loops.

options.text: You build the first list from what stops supply, and have the juniors mark what they know.
options.fb: Two days of work by people who are staying, producing a document he can correct rather than compose. The list is the ask.

options.text: You ask him to list what matters, since he is the only one who knows.
options.fb: A blank sheet handed to a man who has never written any of it down. He will start at loop one and he will be honest about that.

options.text: You take the vendor's network-first method, which is systematic.
options.fb: Systematic and paced for nine months. He leaves in five, and the method does not know which loops he alone understands.

options.text: You start with the eleven documented loops and work outwards from them, since that is the only written ground there is.
options.fb: The eleven are documented precisely because they were the easy ones.

steps.prompt: He has said twice, lightly, that «it will all be fine» and once that nobody asked him in forty years. He is due to leave on a fixed date and has not offered to stay. You are about to ask him for the thing he was never asked for.

options.text: You bring the list, say what it is for, and ask him to correct it rather than write it.
options.fb: Correcting is an expert's job and writing is a chore. The second sentence he hears decides which of the two this becomes.

options.text: You ask him to stay on part-time after the date, at the consultancy rate.
options.fb: He may agree, and the family of problem this belongs to is the one where continuity becomes one man's convenience for another year.

options.text: You tell him plainly that without his knowledge the upgrade cannot be specified and the works are at risk.
options.fb: True, and it puts the whole plant on a man three months from retirement. He has heard it as a compliment for forty years — which is why nothing is written down.

options.text: You have the juniors shadow him for his last months and take notes.
options.fb: Shadowing captures what happens to come up. What is not touched in five months is not captured at all.

steps.prompt: He corrects the list in an afternoon: twenty-two loops matter, four of them badly. Then he mentions a cupboard of his own notebooks, and separately the site has a 1990s drawing set that everyone says is wrong.

options.text: You go through his notebooks alongside him while he can still read his own shorthand and margin markings.
options.fb: Forty years of notes are worth nothing in five months without their author. The drawings will still be there in June; he will not.

options.text: You have the drawing set checked against the plant loop by loop.
options.fb: Worth doing and it is a job for the juniors, not for the five months in which he is still here.

options.text: You have the juniors photograph and index the notebooks while he works through the list with you.
options.fb: The index is useful and it is not the reading: the pages are shorthand, and the only person who can read them is in the room doing something else.

options.text: You send both the notebooks and the drawings to the vendor to incorporate into the reverse-engineering.
options.fb: The vendor's nine months start after the material is delivered, and the material is unreadable without him.

B1a.prompt: Two weeks into the notebooks he is enjoying himself and the sessions are running long. The juniors are not in them: he answers faster without an audience, and the recordings are piling up unwatched.

options.text: You put one junior in each session with a task of their own, and accept that it runs slower.
options.fb: Recordings preserve answers; a junior who asked the question keeps the reasoning. The slower session is the one that survives him.

options.text: You keep the pace and have the juniors work through the recordings afterwards, so nothing slows while he is willing.
options.fb: More material captured and nobody in the room to ask the second question, which is where the reasoning lives.

options.text: You let him work alone and write it up himself, since he is finally engaged.
options.fb: He has never written it down in forty years, and enjoying the talking is not the same as being willing to write.

B1b.prompt: The drawing check comes back: the 1990s set is right about the pipework and wrong about the control logic almost everywhere. Everyone who said «it is wrong» was talking about a different part of it than everyone else.

options.text: You split the set into the part that can be trusted and the part that cannot, and say so on the drawings themselves.
options.fb: «It is wrong» kept a usable document out of use for twenty years. Marking which half is which is the whole value of the check.

options.text: You commission a new drawing set from the vendor.
options.fb: Nine months and the price of the reverse-engineering, for a document half of which you already have.

options.text: You use the pipework and have him confirm the logic loop by loop.
options.fb: Sound, and it spends his remaining weeks confirming drawings rather than explaining the twenty-two loops that matter.

steps.prompt: Of the twenty-two loops, four behave differently in winter, and his explanation of one of them contradicts the plant's own trend data from two winters ago.

options.text: You put the trend in front of him and ask what he saw that it does not show.
options.fb: He has been right for forty years and the data has been recording for two. The contradiction is a question for him, not a verdict on him.

options.text: You take the trend data, since it is a record rather than a recollection and the upgrade will be specified against records.
options.fb: The record covers two winters of a system he has run through forty. It is thinner evidence, better formatted.

options.text: You record both and mark the loop as unresolved.
options.fb: Honest and it leaves the one loop where his knowledge and the instruments disagree exactly as unresolved as it is now.

options.text: You have the juniors run a winter test on the loop next season.
options.fb: Next season is after he leaves, and the test will be designed by people who could not ask him what to look for.

steps.prompt: Three months left with him. The twenty-two loops will take about that, if nothing else is asked of him. The plant manager wants him for two weeks of the summer outage, and the vendor wants a week of his time for the upgrade specification.

options.text: You protect the loops and offer the vendor written answers instead of a week of him.
options.fb: The outage happens every year and the specification can be answered on paper. The loops are the only thing that leaves the site in December.

options.text: You give the vendor the week, since the specification is the mandated deliverable.
options.fb: The mandate has fourteen months and he has three. Spending scarce time on the deadline that is further away.

options.text: You split his time evenly across all three claims.
options.fb: Everyone gets a third of a man and the twenty-two loops become fifteen, chosen by whoever asked last.

options.text: You give the plant manager the outage, since a failed outage stops supply now.
options.fb: The outage has been run by three people before him and will be again. He is the only source of the loops.

steps.prompt: The regulator's upgrade timetable assumes a specification at month six. On the current pace the logic will not be mapped until month eight, and the vendor's nine months would start from there.

options.text: You tell the regulator now what the timetable depends on and what date you can defend.
options.fb: A date that slips before it is announced is a plan; a date that slips after is a failure. The difference is made in the month you choose to write.

options.text: You hold the announcement until the twenty-two loops are done and the new date is certain.
options.fb: Certainty at month eight, announced two months after the milestone everyone else was planning around.

options.text: You compress the capture to hit month six, taking the loops in less depth.
options.fb: Depth is the only thing you are buying with his last months, and it is what you propose to spend.

options.text: You ask the vendor whether nine months can be shortened if the logic arrives clean.
options.fb: A fair question with a predictable answer, asked instead of the one conversation that is yours to have.

B2a.prompt: The regulator takes the new date without difficulty and asks, reasonably, what stops this happening again. The honest answer is that nothing does: two other people at the works hold as much undocumented knowledge as he does.

options.text: You say so, and offer the capture method you have just built as the answer for the other two.
options.fb: The question was about the next time. Answering it with a method you have already run beats answering it with an intention.

options.text: You say the utility has learned the lesson and will document as it goes from now on.
options.fb: The sentence every organisation says after this happens, offered to a regulator who has heard it from all of them.

options.text: You name the two and commit to a date for each.
options.fb: Specific and it commits two people to a programme neither has been asked about.

B2b.prompt: The month-six milestone is still in everybody's plan — the plant manager's, the vendor's, the juniors' — and you now know it will not be met. One of the juniors asks you directly whether the date is real.

options.text: You correct the plan with the people whose work depends on it first, and take the date to the regulator the same week.
options.fb: Three plans rest on the milestone and one of them is the regulator's. Correcting the ones that schedule people, then the one that schedules paperwork, is the order that loses the least work.

options.text: You tell her the date is under review and keep the plan unchanged until the new one is fixed.
options.fb: Two weeks of three teams working to a date you know is gone, told to the person whose job is to bring you bad numbers early.

options.text: You freeze all three plans until the capture is finished and a real date exists.
options.fb: Honest and expensive: the vendor's people stand down for six weeks and come back at the price of a remobilisation.

steps.prompt: Six weeks left. Four of the twenty-two loops are the ones he called bad, and they are the slowest to explain. The other eighteen are half done and could all be finished in time.

options.text: You take the four first and accept that some of the eighteen stay unfinished.
options.fb: The eighteen can be reconstructed from the plant by people who are staying. The four are the ones that exist only in his head, and that is the definition of what to spend the last weeks on.

options.text: You finish the eighteen, so that the written record is complete as far as it goes.
options.fb: A complete record of the recoverable part, and nothing at all of the part that is not recoverable.

options.text: You keep both running and see how far you get.
options.fb: Six weeks is short enough that «see how far» is decided by whichever session overruns.

options.text: You bring the vendor in for the four, so a specialist captures the hardest ones.
options.fb: A specialist in their system, not in his. The four are hard because of what he did to them in 1988.

steps.prompt: In his last week he offers to come back «if anything comes up». The plant manager wants that in writing as a retainer; the finance director points out that a retainer is a standing invitation to stop trying.

options.text: You take a fixed number of paid days with an expiry date, and name what they are for.
options.fb: An open line makes his return the answer to every problem; a closed one loses the only expert. A bounded number of days is neither.

options.text: You take his offer informally and call him when needed.
options.fb: Informal works until the day it does not, and then it is a favour asked of a man with no obligation.

options.text: You decline, so the team is forced to become self-sufficient from the first week rather than the first winter.
options.fb: Self-sufficiency by deprivation, in a plant where four loops are documented from a single set of sessions.

options.text: You put him on a twelve-month retainer at £900 a day.
options.fb: It buys certainty and hands the works a reason not to learn for a year.

steps.prompt: He has gone. The capture covers the four bad loops and fourteen of the eighteen. The vendor now quotes the reverse-engineering at £480,000 for everything, or a third of that for the loops that were never captured — but only if the utility warrants that the captured material is accurate.

options.text: You take the partial scope and warrant only the recorded sessions, naming the four gaps.
options.fb: A warranty you can honour on eighteen loops is worth more than a blanket one you cannot. Naming the gap is what makes the cheaper scope safe to sign.

options.text: You take the full scope, so nothing rests on a warranty the utility cannot really give.
options.fb: Safe, and it spends three hundred and twenty thousand pounds re-deriving what he already told you.

options.text: You take the partial scope and warrant the lot, since the sessions were recorded.
options.fb: Recordings are evidence of what was said, not of whether it was right — and one of those loops flatly contradicted the trend data.

options.text: You take the partial scope and ask the juniors to verify the captured material first.
options.fb: Verification takes a winter, and the upgrade has fourteen months of which eight are gone.

B3a.prompt: The junior who sat in every session is now the person the shift rings at two in the morning. She is answering well and she has started saying «I think» about things she was certain of a month ago.

options.text: You take the night calls together for a month and write down what she gets asked.
options.fb: She is becoming the next single point of failure, and the log of what she is actually asked is the list nobody had when he left.

options.text: You tell her she is doing well and that the uncertainty is normal.
options.fb: True and it leaves her alone with the calls, which is the situation you are supposed to be dismantling.

options.text: You route the night calls to the vendor's support line for six months while she writes up what she knows.
options.fb: It protects her and moves the knowledge back outside the utility, which is where this began.

B3b.prompt: The full reverse-engineering is under way and the vendor's first output contradicts what he told the sessions on two of the four bad loops. Both versions are plausible and he is not answering his phone this month.

options.text: You test both readings on the plant during the next low-load window, before either goes into the specification.
options.fb: Two plausible accounts and a plant that can settle it. The specification is the last place to discover which one was right.

options.text: You take the vendor's version, since it is systematic, current and produced by people who will still be here.
options.fb: Systematic about the system as it is drawn, which is the thing forty years of undrawn changes have been quietly editing.

options.text: You take his version, since he ran the plant for forty years.
options.fb: He also told you one loop's behaviour that the trend data flatly contradicts, and that was before he stopped answering.

title: The Pilot That Worked
note: МАКЕТ. Тексты и веса наши, ни одной формулировки PrepMatter (Ф3). Развилки по РОДУ хода (Ф21). Связывающее — ДОКАЗАТЕЛЬСТВО, КОТОРОЕ НЕ МАСШТАБИРУЕТСЯ: пилот измерен честно и число настоящее, но принадлежит сорока домам, отобранным по признаку «здесь есть что снимать». Против двенадцати семей: 01 данные · 02 календарь · 03 окно · 04 чужие активы · 05 необратимость · 06 доверие · 07 деньги с датой · 08 очередь · 09 два правила · 10 ресурс во времени · 11 успех ломает механизм · 12 знание в одном человеке. Ключ H>A>S>D: обследование стоит последним, потому что оно медленнее двери — восемь месяцев против шестнадцати недель.

intro.head: Welcome to the Sustainable Futures Lab
intro.body: You have joined a small team advising a housing association. You will make thirteen decisions. There is one clock for all of them, and you cannot go back.

intro.head: Background
intro.body: Ashfield Homes owns 3,000 homes and has just been awarded £38m to retrofit them. The award was won on a pilot: 40 homes on the Wyre estate, where measured heat demand fell 54 per cent after wall insulation, new ventilation and a heat pump. The grant conditions set a programme-average saving of 40 per cent and take back £9m if it is missed. The Wyre homes are solid-walled 1930s stock. Of what is left, 260 are built the same way and 2,700 are 1970s cavity, where the same work has far less to remove. The award may be restated once and the window closes in sixteen weeks. A full stock survey takes eight months.
intro.mission: Your mission: turn a number that was true in forty homes into a programme that is true in three thousand.

priorities.label: Decide what the programme can promise once the stock is not the pilot's stock
Use the one restatement the award allows, before the window closes
Tell the residents' board what the pilot number does and does not cover
Survey the remaining stock house by house, which takes eight months

steps.prompt: Put these four actions in the order you would take them, starting with the one you would do first.
steps.why:
Связывающее — **доказательство, которое не масштабируется**. Пилот измерен честно, и пятьдесят четыре процента — настоящее число; беда в том, что оно принадлежит сорока домам, отобранным ровно по признаку «здесь есть что снимать». Новая семья: в «Paid to Fail» механизм ломал собственный успех, здесь успех верен и просто **не переносится**, а выборка уже потрачена и второй раз её не собрать.
Первым — **что мы обещаем**. Это не измерение и не переговоры, это решение о форме обязательства: одно среднее по всему фонду или отдельная цифра на каждый тип постройки. Форма определяет всё дальнейшее — и что просить у фонда, и что говорить жильцам, и что вообще имеет смысл обследовать. Пока обещание сформулировано как одно среднее, любая новая цифра только ухудшает его.
Возражение сильное, и оно не про данные: **первым должен идти фонд**, потому что окно в шестнадцать недель задано снаружи и никем внутри не двигается, а пересмотр бывает один раз. Возражение верно по ставке и неверно по порядку. Уведомление **необратимо**: подаётся однажды и не переподаётся. Поэтому первым решается не «когда подать», а **что именно подаём** — одно среднее по трём тысячам домов или цифру на каждый тип постройки. Решение стоит одного совещания, окно — шестнадцати недель, и порядок между ними не спорный.
Фонд вторым: пересмотр подаётся с разбивкой по типам, а не с обследованием. Жильцы третьими **по инициативе** — но не по реакции: если цифра уходит к ним раньше нас, разговор становится срочным принудительно, и это нормальная цена, а не ошибка порядка. Обследование последним: восемь месяцев против шестнадцати недель — оно физически не успевает к двери и потому **уточняет уже поданное**, а не готовит его. Быстрая аналитика — разбивка, пересчёт пилота, разбор разброса — не обследование и идёт по ходу дела.

feedback.top: You decide the shape of the promise first, which is what makes the restatement filable inside the window.
feedback.mid: Workable: the restatement is not last, and the programme will reach the funder with something other than the pilot number.
feedback.low: This order waits for a survey that lands months after the one window the award allows.

steps.prompt: The board wants the restatement to hold 40 per cent, on the view that the award was won on it. The programme director wants it dropped to what cavity stock can carry. The stock condition database holds an archetype split for every home and takes three days to pull.

options.text: You restate the target as a figure per archetype and let the programme average fall out of the mix.
options.fb: One number for three thousand mixed homes is a promise about the mix, not about the work. Per archetype, every later argument is about one type of house at a time.

options.text: You hold 40 per cent and add whatever measures close the gap on cavity stock.
options.fb: Defensible and expensive: the gap on 2,700 homes gets closed with money that was scoped for insulation, and the mix is still unnamed.

options.text: You drop the programme target to what the cavity stock will give, since that is most of the stock.
options.fb: Honest about the majority and it throws away the 260 homes where the pilot figure genuinely applies.

options.text: You leave the target alone and manage the shortfall at the end, when outturn is known.
options.fb: The clawback is £9m and it is assessed on outturn. Managing it at the end means finding out at the end.

steps.prompt: The restatement is a one-page notice, filed once. It restates how the target is expressed, not what the pilot measured. The funding officer says off the record that a notice arriving without evidence is normally refused, and that refusals cannot be appealed. The archetype split lands in three days; the survey does not.

options.text: You file in week six on the archetype split, naming the survey as what will refine it.
options.fb: The split is evidence — it is the whole stock, classified, from the association's own records. The survey adds precision to a notice that is already in.

options.text: You write to the officer first and ask what evidence a restatement is expected to carry.
options.fb: A good letter and a slow one. The answer will arrive, and it will describe a general case rather than this stock.

options.text: You file this week on the pilot data alone, so that the notice is in before anything else moves.
options.fb: Speed spent on the one page you cannot send twice. The pilot data is exactly what the restatement exists to correct.

options.text: You wait for the survey, because a refused notice cannot be appealed.
options.fb: Eight months against sixteen weeks. Waiting does not protect the notice, it deletes it.

steps.prompt: The archetype split lands, and two other things surface with it. The pilot's 54 per cent is measured against the two years before the work, when the Wyre estate was billed on estimates rather than meters. And the pilot crew of twelve came from one contractor, who has since closed.

options.text: You have the pilot saving re-based on metered consumption before it is quoted anywhere else.
options.fb: The re-basing is half a day of arithmetic on records the association already holds, and every document from here quotes whichever figure you fix now.
leads: мерная сторона пилота взята в работу

options.text: You establish what the pilot crew did differently and what it costs to buy that from anyone else.
options.fb: The right question about delivery, asked while the baseline under the whole business case is still the wrong one.

options.text: You have the pilot homes metered for a further year, so the baseline rests on more than the billing record.
options.fb: Another year is better evidence and it arrives next autumn. The re-basing you can do this week uses records that already exist.
leads: мерная сторона пилота взята в работу

options.text: You take the pilot package as a product and put it out to tender on price.
options.fb: The package is the easy half of what the pilot did. What made it work was the order the work was done in, and no tender document asks for that.

B1a.prompt: The re-basing gets done either way — it is half a day on records that already exist — and it puts the pilot at 46 per cent rather than 54. The residents' board hears the corrected figure from a contractor before you brief them, and reads it as the programme being quietly cut.

options.text: You take both figures to the board yourself and show which homes each one belongs to.
options.fb: Two numbers with an address attached are a technical correction. Two numbers without one are a retreat.

options.text: You brief the board's chair and let them carry the correction to the rest.
options.fb: Faster, and the chair will be asked the question you should be answering: which figure applies to my house.

options.text: You hold the correction until the notice is filed, so that one message goes out.
options.fb: They already have the number. What is being held back now is the explanation.

needs: мерная сторона пилота взята в работу

B1b.prompt: The crew's difference turns out to be sequence: they surveyed, insulated and commissioned each home inside one visit, with one team. The three contractors still working in the region quote for that as a premium and none of them has done it at volume.

options.text: You put the sequence into the specification and price it as the thing being bought.
options.fb: What the pilot proved was a way of working, not a product. Buying the product and dropping the sequence buys the smaller half.

options.text: You split the work into trades as usual and add a coordinator to hold the sequence.
options.fb: A coordinator between three contractors owns the sequence and controls none of it.

options.text: You take the cheapest trade-by-trade price and treat the pilot premium as a one-off.
options.fb: The premium was the mechanism. Removing it removes the result and keeps the target.

steps.prompt: Two readings of the cavity stock arrive. The energy assessments, done on a desktop model, put cavity homes at 25 per cent. Six homes fitted last year by another association came in far better than that, and all six had been re-roofed first.

options.text: You treat the six as a lead about roofs rather than as a result about cavities.
options.fb: Six homes that share one prior intervention are a hypothesis with a name. Averaged into the model, they are noise.

options.text: You use the desktop model and note the six as an upside to be tested later.
options.fb: The model is defensible and it has never seen a re-roofed cavity home. The upside is now filed where nobody will act on it.

options.text: You average the two readings, since one is modelled and one is measured.
options.fb: The average of a model and six houses is a number with no owner and no way to be wrong.

options.text: You take the six as the better evidence, because they are measured and the model is not.
options.fb: Six homes chosen by another association for their own reasons is the same mistake the pilot already made, one size smaller.

steps.prompt: £38m will do the full pilot package in 860 homes — the 260 solid-walled ones and 600 others — or a lighter package across nearly all 3,000. The board reads the grant conditions as an average and the residents read them as a queue.

options.text: You buy the full package where it earns its cost and the light package everywhere else.
options.fb: The mix is the decision. A single package across mixed stock overpays on one archetype and underdelivers on the other.

options.text: You go deep on the 260 solid-wall homes first and hold the rest until outturn is known.
options.fb: It banks the saving that is certain, and it leaves 2,700 households watching a programme that is not for them.

options.text: You go wide with the light package, because the average is what the clawback is measured on.
options.fb: Wide and thin can still hit an average, and it spends the one award on work nobody will fund the second half of.

options.text: You split the money evenly by area office, so that each part of the stock gets its share.
options.fb: Fairness by geography against a target measured in heat. The offices do not have the same houses.

steps.prompt: The funder replies. The per-archetype restatement is accepted in principle, on one condition: the association names a programme average now and accepts the clawback against it. The archetype table produces a figure well below 40, and moving that gap is what the restatement exists for.

options.text: You name 27 per cent, attach the mix that produces it, and show what each archetype contributes.
options.fb: A lower number with its arithmetic underneath is harder to refuse than a higher one with nothing. The mix is what makes 27 a finding rather than a retreat.
leads: среднее названо вместе с составом работ

options.text: You name 40 per cent and keep the mix free, so delivery can find a way to it.
options.fb: Flexibility bought against a number the stock does not produce. The clawback does not care which part moved.
leads: среднее названо, состав работ оставлен открытым

options.text: You name the figure the table produces and keep the mix to yourself, so delivery is not boxed in.
options.fb: The number is right and it arrives naked. A funder who cannot see what produces it has nothing to hold you to except the number.
leads: среднее названо, состав работ оставлен открытым

options.text: You name 40 per cent and ask for the clawback to be assessed once at the end rather than yearly.
options.fb: A softer penalty on a number the mix does not produce. The assessment date moves; the arithmetic does not.
leads: среднее названо, состав работ оставлен открытым

B2a.prompt: With the mix on the notice, the delivery team finds that two of the four area offices cannot staff their share of the deep package this year. Changing the mix now means writing to the funder in the same quarter you wrote to them last.

options.text: You move the deep work to the offices that can staff it and keep the mix arithmetic unchanged.
options.fb: The commitment was about the mix of houses, not the mix of offices. Rearranging within it needs no letter.

options.text: You write to the funder describing the staffing constraint and the revised sequence.
options.fb: Correct instinct, wrong trigger: nothing in the notice has changed, and a letter that says nothing invites a reply that does.

options.text: You hold the sequence and let the two offices run late, since the notice is what binds.
options.fb: Late in two of four offices is the average missed, which is the only thing the notice binds.

needs: среднее названо вместе с составом работ

B2b.prompt: With the mix left open, the four area offices each build their own programme. Three of them choose the light package everywhere, which is the easiest to procure, and the fourth has already tendered the deep one.

options.text: You set the mix centrally now and let the offices choose sequence within it.
options.fb: What was left open has been closed by whoever moved first. Setting it now costs one tender; setting it in a year costs the average.

options.text: You let the fourth office proceed and treat it as the deep sample for the whole programme.
options.fb: One office's tender becomes the evidence base for three thousand homes. That is where this scenario started.

options.text: You leave the offices to it and reconcile at the halfway review.
options.fb: By the halfway review three quarters of the stock has had the light package and the average is arithmetic, not a choice.

needs: среднее названо, состав работ оставлен открытым

steps.prompt: Delivery can start in eight weeks, and the restated target has its first annual return twelve months after that. The heat pumps have a nine-month lead time, the insulation contractors are free now, and a home insulated before its pump is sized needs a smaller pump.

options.text: You insulate first and size the pumps against the improved fabric.
options.fb: Sizing against the house you will have rather than the house you have is the cheapest decision in the programme, and it is only available in this order. It also puts fabric-only homes on meter inside the twelve months.

options.text: You order pumps now against current fabric so the lead time runs in parallel with insulation.
options.fb: Nine months saved and every pump one size too big, paid for once in capital and again in running cost.

options.text: You do the fabric and the pump in one visit per home.
options.fb: One visit is the cheaper way to work and it makes every home wait nine months for its pump. The first tranche has to be on meter before the annual return.

options.text: You start with the homes whose residents have already asked, so the programme visibly begins.
options.fb: A queue by request order is a queue by confidence, and it will not resemble the stock.

steps.prompt: The first 120 homes to complete are solid-walled, fabric and ventilation only, with pumps to follow. Their metered demand is down 31 per cent on average, and the spread is wide: the best third is close to the re-based pilot figure and the worst third has barely moved. Neither archetype nor contractor nor completion date explains it.

options.text: You go and look at four homes from each third before the next tranche is specified.
options.fb: The spread is the finding and no field in the record explains it. Twelve site visits are the cheapest instrument you have.

options.text: You report the 31 per cent and flag the spread as a matter for the halfway review.
options.fb: Accurate reporting, and the next tranche is specified before the review reads it.

options.text: You investigate the worst third, since that is where the average is lost.
options.fb: Reasonable and half-blind: without the best third there is nothing to compare the worst one against.

options.text: You report the average and let the sample grow, since this is early.
options.fb: A spread this wide is not noise about the mean, it is evidence that two different things are happening.

steps.prompt: The visits explain it: in the worst third the ventilation was signed off on paper but never balanced on site, and residents had turned it off within a week because of the noise. Two ways of recovering the average are open and they differ in kind.

options.text: You re-open the completed homes, commission the ventilation properly and explain it to each household.
options.fb: Going back into finished homes is expensive and it is the only route that recovers the homes already spent.
leads: программа возвращается в уже сделанные дома

options.text: You leave the completed homes and put the fix into the specification for everything still to come.
options.fb: Cheaper, faster, and it writes off the third of the completed stock that the residents there live in.
leads: сделанные дома оставлены как есть, исправление уходит вперёд

options.text: You go back into the homes and take the cost from the contingency rather than the programme.
options.fb: The right move funded from the wrong place: the contingency is what pays for the next surprise, and there will be one.
leads: программа возвращается в уже сделанные дома

options.text: You record the homes as complete and recover the average from the remaining tranches.
options.fb: Arithmetically possible and it means those households paid for the programme's learning with their own winter.
leads: сделанные дома оставлены как есть, исправление уходит вперёд

B3a.prompt: Going back costs more than the contingency holds. The funder's monitoring officer asks, in a routine call, whether the programme is on track for the average it named.

options.text: You tell them what the visits found, what it costs to put right, and what the average looks like either way.
options.fb: They will read it in the annual return regardless. The difference between hearing it now and reading it then is whether the association is the one explaining it.

options.text: You say the programme is on track, which it is once the rework lands, and report the detail at the quarterly.
options.fb: True with a condition attached, told without the condition. The quarterly is where they find out you knew in the call.

options.text: You answer the question as asked and volunteer nothing, since the call is routine.
options.fb: Routine calls are how monitoring officers find out things early enough to help.

needs: программа возвращается в уже сделанные дома

B3b.prompt: Nothing goes back into the houses already finished. Households there hear from neighbours that later work will carry something theirs did not, and the residents' board asks for a pause until that is settled.

options.text: You keep the programme running and put a dated commitment to return to the completed homes in front of the board.
options.fb: A pause costs the whole programme its contractors. A date is the only thing that answers what was actually asked.

options.text: You pause for a month while the board and the association agree what happens to the completed homes.
options.fb: It answers the board and it hands the schedule to three contractors who have other work.

options.text: You explain that the completed homes met the standard in force at the time.
options.fb: Correct, and it tells people whose ventilation does not run that their house was a stage in a process.

needs: сделанные дома оставлены как есть, исправление уходит вперёд

title: Signed Before You Came
note: МАКЕТ. Тексты и веса наши, ни одной формулировки PrepMatter (Ф3). Развилки по РОДУ хода (Ф21). Связывающее — ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬСТВО, ВЗЯТОЕ ДО ТЕБЯ: пятнадцатилетний договор с обязательным объёмом, подписанный людьми, которых уже нет. Снять нельзя, нарушить нельзя — можно только переоценить, и экономия тепла делает разрыв больше, а не меньше. Против тринадцати семей: 01 данные · 02 календарь · 03 окно · 04 чужие активы · 05 необратимость · 06 доверие · 07 деньги с датой · 08 очередь · 09 два правила · 10 ресурс во времени · 11 успех ломает механизм · 12 знание в одном человеке · 13 доказательство не масштабируется. Ключ D>H>S>A: договор читается первым, потому что два года спора шли по трём разным его версиям.

words: The eight it does not take
verbal: The eight it does not take

intro.head: Welcome to the Sustainable Futures Lab
intro.body: You have joined a small team advising a hospital trust. You will make thirteen decisions. There is one clock for all of them, and you cannot go back.

intro.head: Background
intro.body: Brantham Teaching Hospital buys its heat under a fifteen-year energy contract signed five years ago by people who have all since left. The contract is take or pay: 82 GWh of heat a year at £41 a MWh, whether the hospital burns it or not. The hospital now uses 74 and pays for all 82. The eight it does not take cost £328,000 a year, and that figure grows with every ward the trust makes more efficient. The board has committed publicly to halving emissions. There is a break at year ten and it costs £6.4m. 400 metres away, a scheme of 900 homes freezes its detailed design in five months.
intro.mission: Your mission: turn heat the hospital is obliged to buy into heat that somebody actually needs.

priorities.label: Establish what the contract obliges, permits and forbids, end to end
Decide what the hospital does with heat it must pay for and cannot use
Reach the housing scheme before its heating is designed without you
Put a transfer to the supplier, whose consent the contract requires

steps.prompt: Put these four actions in the order you would take them, starting with the one you would do first.
steps.why:
Связывающее — **обязательство, взятое до тебя**. Договор подписан пять лет назад людьми, которых в тресте уже нет; снять его нельзя, нарушить нельзя, и — это и есть ловушка — **экономия тепла делает разрыв больше, а не меньше**. Новая семья: в «Cold Chain Reset» рычага не было над чужими активами, здесь актив свой, а связаны руки чужой подписью, и единственное доступное действие — переоценить, а не отменить.
Первым — **прочтение**. Спор внутри треста идёт второй год, и все три стороны спорят по разным документам: финансы по краткому изложению, эксплуатация по изменению третьего года, юристы по оригиналу без двух приложений. Пока не прочитано, что договор **разрешает**, любое решение — догадка. Чтение стоит двух недель.
Возражение сильное: **у схемы рядом заморозка проекта через пять месяцев**, и если опоздать, тепло будет некому отдать ещё пятнадцать лет. Возражение верное по ставке и неверное по порядку. Разговор со схемой бывает один: приходят с тем, что можешь предложить, а не с тем, что, может быть, разрешено. Две недели чтения из пяти месяцев — не потеря, а условие того, что разговор состоится по существу.
Решение о судьбе объёма вторым: без него не с чем идти. Схема третьей — у неё дата, и дата ближе, чем годовой пересмотр. Поставщик последним, и это не пренебрежение: его согласие требуется на **конкретную** передачу конкретному получателю, а до третьего шага получателя не существует.

feedback.top: You read the document before arguing about it, which is what turns a two-year dispute into a question with an answer.
feedback.mid: Workable: the contract is not last, and the trust will know what it may do before it offers to do it.
feedback.low: This order opens negotiations about a contract nobody in the room has read to the end.

steps.prompt: The dispute inside the trust is in its second year and none of the three parties to it knows the others are reading different documents. Finance works from a summary written at signature, estates from a variation dated year three, legal from the original with two schedules missing.

options.text: You put all three round one complete copy and list what was decided against text not in force.
options.fb: The versions are not the finding. Two years of decisions taken against the wrong one are, and some of them can still be unwound.

options.text: You have legal opine on the take-or-pay clause, which is where the money sits.
options.fb: The clause everyone argues about is rarely the clause that decides, and it sits in the version that is missing two schedules.

options.text: You work from the summary and the variation, on the view that between them they cover the operative terms.
options.fb: A summary is somebody's reading of a document, written by somebody who has left.

options.text: You ask the supplier for their copy, which will be complete.
options.fb: It will be complete and it will be theirs. The first thing the trust learns about its own position arrives from the counterparty.
